solution_steps.text: (c) This is extrapolation because 2025 (\( t = 15 \)) is outside the data range (\( t = 0 \) to \( t = 9 \)). Predictions outside the data range are less reliable.

problems.question_html:
The table shows the number of subscribers (in thousands) to a streaming service:

Months since launch036912
Subscribers (thousands)10183258104

(a) Verify that the data approximately fits an exponential model by computing ratios over 3-month intervals.

(b) Build an exponential model \( S(t) = ab^t \) where \( t \) is months, using \( S(0) = 10 \) and the average ratio from part (a). Round \( b \) to three decimal places.

(c) According to your model, how many subscribers would the service have after 18 months? Round to the nearest thousand.

hints.text: Compute each ratio \( \frac{S(t+3)}{S(t)} \) to check for a constant pattern.
Average 3-month ratio is about 1.8. The monthly base is \( 1.8^{1/3} \approx 1.216 \). For 18 months, compute \( 10 \cdot (1.216)^{18} \).

solution_steps.text: (b) Using 1.8 as the 3-month factor: \( b = 1.8^{1/3} \approx 1.216 \). Model: \( S(t) = 10 \cdot (1.216)^t \).

concepts.title: Competing Function Model Validation
concepts.content_html:
Competing Function Model Validation

When modeling real-world data, multiple function types may seem reasonable. We need systematic methods to determine which model best fits the data and to assess the quality of our predictions.

Comparing Models

Common competing models include:

  • Linear: \( f(x) = mx + b \) — appropriate when data shows a constant rate of change
  • Exponential: \( g(x) = ab^x \) — appropriate when data shows a constant ratio
  • Other: quadratic, power, or logarithmic models may also be considered

To choose between models, examine the data for patterns in differences and ratios, use regression tools, and analyze how well each model fits the observed values.

Residuals

A residual is the difference between an observed value and the value predicted by a model:

\[ \text{residual} = \text{observed} - \text{predicted} \]
  • A positive residual means the model underestimates the actual value.
  • A negative residual means the model overestimates the actual value.
Key Idea: A good model has residuals that are small in magnitude and show no clear pattern when plotted. If the residual plot shows a curved pattern, a different model type may be more appropriate.

Over- and Underestimates

When a model predicts a value that is higher than the actual value, we say the model overestimates. When it predicts lower, it underestimates.

The sign of the residual directly tells you:

  • Residual \( > 0 \): underestimate (actual \( > \) predicted)
  • Residual \( < 0 \): overestimate (actual \( < \) predicted)
AP Exam Tip: The AP exam may ask about the sign of a residual and whether a model overestimates or underestimates at a particular point. The sign of the residual is assessed content. However, the "sign of the error" (a different concept) is not assessed. Focus on residual = observed minus predicted.

Worked Example

A linear model predicts that a city will have 45,000 residents in 2025. The actual count is 47,200. Compute the residual and interpret it.

Residual \( = 47{,}200 - 45{,}000 = 2{,}200 \). The residual is positive, meaning the linear model underestimates the population by 2,200 people.

problems.question_html: A model predicts that a plant will be 12 cm tall on day 10. The actual height is 14 cm. What is the residual?

hints.text: Residual = observed - predicted.
Residual = \( 14 - 12 = 2 \). Positive residual means the model underestimated.

solution_steps.text: The positive residual indicates the model underestimates the actual height by 2 cm.

problems.question_html: A model predicts a value of 250. The observed value is 230. The model:

hints.text: Compare the predicted value to the observed value.
Predicted (250) > Observed (230). The model overestimates. Residual = \( 230 - 250 = -20 \).

solution_steps.text: Residual = \( 230 - 250 = -20 \). The negative residual means overestimate.
The model overestimates the actual value by 20.

problems.question_html: A model predicts \( \hat{y} = 85 \) for a data point where the observed value is \( y = 79 \). What is the residual?

hints.text: Residual = observed - predicted.

solution_steps.text: The negative residual means the model overestimates at this point.

problems.question_html: If a residual is positive, the model __________ the actual value. (Enter overestimates or underestimates.)

hints.text: A positive residual means observed > predicted.
If observed > predicted, the model predicted too low, so it underestimates.

solution_steps.text: Since the predicted value is lower than actual, the model underestimates.

problems.question_html: Data points are modeled with both a linear and an exponential function. The residual plot for the linear model shows a clear curved pattern, while the residual plot for the exponential model shows randomly scattered points. Which conclusion is most appropriate?

choices.text: The linear model is better because it is simpler
The exponential model is more appropriate because its residuals show no pattern

hints.text: A good model has residuals that appear random with no clear pattern.
A curved pattern in residuals suggests the model type is wrong. Random residuals suggest a good fit.

solution_steps.text: A curved pattern in the linear model's residuals indicates systematic error, meaning a linear model is inappropriate.
Random scatter in the exponential model's residuals suggests it captures the data's pattern well. The exponential model is more appropriate.

problems.question_html:
The table shows actual vs. predicted values from a model:

\( x \)12345
Actual1022355270
Predicted1220324868

At which \( x \)-value does the model most underestimate the actual value?

hints.text: Compute residuals (actual - predicted) for each point. The largest positive residual corresponds to the greatest underestimate.
Residuals: \( -2, 2, 3, 4, 2 \). The largest positive residual is 4, at \( x = 4 \).

solution_steps.text: The largest positive residual is 4 at \( x = 4 \), meaning the model most underestimates there.

problems.question_html: A linear model gives residuals of \( 3, -1, -4, 5, -2 \) at five data points. What is the sum of the residuals?

solution_steps.text: Note: For a least-squares regression line, the sum of residuals is always 0. A sum of 1 suggests this model is not the least-squares fit.

problems.question_html: An exponential model predicts \( f(3) = 40 \). The actual data value at \( x = 3 \) is \( 35 \). What is the residual, and does the model overestimate or underestimate?

hints.text: Compute residual = observed - predicted. Then interpret the sign.
Residual = \( 35 - 40 = -5 \). Negative means the model overestimates.

solution_steps.text: The negative residual means the model overestimates the actual value by 5.

problems.question_html:
A researcher collects the following data on the number of cells in a petri dish:

Hours01234
Cells5085140240400

(a) Fit a linear model using the first and last points. Write the equation and compute the residual at \( t = 2 \).

(b) Fit an exponential model using the first and last points. Write the equation and compute the residual at \( t = 2 \).

(c) Based on the residuals at \( t = 2 \), which model appears to fit the data better at that point? Explain.
problems.correct_answer:
(a) Linear: slope = (400-50)/(4-0) = 87.5. L(t) = 87.5t + 50. L(2) = 225. Residual = 140 - 225 = -85. The linear model overestimates.
(b) Exponential: b^4 = 400/50 = 8, b = 8^(1/4) ≈ 1.682. E(t) = 50 * (1.682)^t. E(2) = 50 * 2.828 ≈ 141.4. Residual = 140 - 141.4 = -1.4.
(c) The exponential model has a much smaller residual at t = 2 (|−1.4| vs |−85|), suggesting it fits the data much better at that point.

hints.text: For each model, use the points \( (0, 50) \) and \( (4, 400) \) to build the equation, then evaluate at \( t = 2 \).
Linear: \( L(2) = 225 \), residual \( = -85 \). Exponential: \( E(2) \approx 141 \), residual \( \approx -1 \). The exponential model is much closer.

solution_steps.text: (c) The exponential residual (\( -1.4 \)) is much smaller in magnitude than the linear residual (\( -85 \)), indicating the exponential model fits better.

problems.question_html:
Two models are used to predict the population of a town (in thousands):

  • Linear model: \( L(t) = 2.5t + 30 \)
  • Exponential model: \( E(t) = 30 \cdot (1.07)^t \)

where \( t \) is years since 2010. The actual population data is:

Year2010201320162019
Population30374657

(a) Compute the residuals for both models at each data point.

(b) Based on your residuals, which model better fits the data? Justify your answer.

(c) Predict the population in 2025 using the better model.
problems.correct_answer:
(a) Linear predictions: L(0)=30, L(3)=37.5, L(6)=45, L(9)=52.5. Residuals: 0, -0.5, 1, 4.5. Exponential predictions: E(0)=30, E(3)=30*1.07^3≈36.75, E(6)=30*1.07^6≈45.01, E(9)=30*1.07^9≈55.16. Residuals: 0, 0.25, 0.99, 1.84.
(b) The exponential model has smaller residuals overall (max |1.84| vs |4.5|), and the linear residuals show an increasing trend, suggesting the exponential model is more appropriate.
(c) 2025 is t=15. E(15) = 30 * 1.07^15 ≈ 30 * 2.759 ≈ 82.8 thousand.

hints.text: Compute predictions from each model at \( t = 0, 3, 6, 9 \) and subtract from actual values.
Compare residual magnitudes and patterns. The exponential model's residuals are smaller and less systematic.

solution_steps.text: (b) The exponential model's residuals are smaller and do not show a clear trend, while the linear model's residuals grow. The exponential model fits better.

concepts.title: Composition of Functions
concepts.content_html:
Composition of Functions

Function composition is the process of applying one function to the output of another. The composition of \( f \) and \( g \) is written:

\[ (f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x)) \]

This means: first apply \( g \) to \( x \), then apply \( f \) to the result.

Evaluating Compositions

To evaluate \( f(g(x)) \):

  1. Compute the inner function: find \( g(x) \)
  2. Use that result as the input to \( f \): compute \( f(g(x)) \)

Note that composition is generally not commutative: \( f(g(x)) \neq g(f(x)) \) in most cases.

Domain of a Composition

The domain of \( f \circ g \) consists of all \( x \) in the domain of \( g \) such that \( g(x) \) is in the domain of \( f \). Both conditions must be satisfied.

Key Idea: When composing a function with itself, \( f(f(x)) \), apply the function twice. When a function is composed with its inverse, the result is the identity function: \( f(f^{-1}(x)) = x \) and \( f^{-1}(f(x)) = x \) (CED EK 2.7.A.4).

Decomposition

Decomposing a function means expressing it as a composition of simpler functions. For example:

If \( h(x) = \sqrt{3x + 1} \), we can write \( h = f \circ g \) where \( g(x) = 3x + 1 \) and \( f(x) = \sqrt{x} \).

Worked Example

Let \( f(x) = 2x + 3 \) and \( g(x) = x^2 \).

Find \( f(g(2)) \):

  1. \( g(2) = 2^2 = 4 \)
  2. \( f(4) = 2(4) + 3 = 11 \)

Find \( g(f(2)) \):

  1. \( f(2) = 2(2) + 3 = 7 \)
  2. \( g(7) = 7^2 = 49 \)

Since \( f(g(2)) = 11 \) and \( g(f(2)) = 49 \), composition is not commutative.

AP Exam Tip: When given a table of values for \( f \) and \( g \), work from the inside out. Find the inner function value first, then use that as input to the outer function. Be careful with the order of composition.

hints.text: Work from the inside out: first find \( g(2) \), then apply \( f \).

problems.question_html:
Using the table below, find \( g(f(1)) \).

\( x \)1234
\( f(x) \)3142
\( g(x) \)4312

hints.text: First find \( f(1) \) from the table, then look up \( g \) of that value.

problems.question_html: Let \( f(x) = x^2 \) and \( g(x) = x - 5 \). What is \( (f \circ g)(3) \)?

hints.text: \( (f \circ g)(3) = f(g(3)) \). Find \( g(3) \) first.

problems.question_html: Let \( f(x) = 2x \) and \( g(x) = x + 3 \). Find \( (g \circ f)(5) \).

hints.text: \( (g \circ f)(5) = g(f(5)) \). Compute \( f(5) \) first.

problems.question_html: Let \( f(x) = x^2 + 1 \) and \( g(x) = 3x \). Which expression equals \( (f \circ g)(x) \)?

hints.text: \( (f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x)) = f(3x) \). Substitute \( 3x \) for \( x \) in \( f \).

problems.question_html: The function \( h(x) = (2x - 5)^3 \) can be written as \( h = f \circ g \). Which pair of functions works?

hints.text: The inner function is applied first. What operation happens "inside" the cube?
The inner function is \( g(x) = 2x - 5 \) (linear part), and the outer function is \( f(x) = x^3 \) (cubing). Then \( f(g(x)) = (2x-5)^3 \).

solution_steps.text: Decompose: the "inside" is \( 2x - 5 \), the "outside" is cubing.
So \( g(x) = 2x - 5 \) and \( f(x) = x^3 \). Check: \( f(g(x)) = (2x - 5)^3 = h(x) \). Correct.

problems.question_html: Let \( f(x) = 4x - 7 \) and \( g(x) = 2x + 1 \). Find \( (f \circ g)(x) \) and simplify.

hints.text: Substitute \( g(x) = 2x + 1 \) into \( f \).

problems.question_html: If \( f(x) = \sqrt{x} \) and \( g(x) = x - 4 \), what is the domain of \( (f \circ g)(x) \)? Express your answer as an inequality.

hints.text: For \( f(g(x)) = \sqrt{g(x)} \) to be defined, \( g(x) \) must be non-negative.
\( g(x) = x - 4 \geq 0 \) gives \( x \geq 4 \).

solution_steps.text: \( (f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x)) = \sqrt{x - 4} \). For this to be defined, \( x - 4 \geq 0 \).

problems.question_html:
Let \( f(x) = 3x + 2 \) and \( g(x) = x^2 - 1 \).

(a) Find \( (f \circ g)(x) \) and \( (g \circ f)(x) \). Simplify each.

(b) Show that \( f \circ g \neq g \circ f \) by evaluating both at \( x = 2 \).

(c) Is there any value of \( x \) for which \( f(g(x)) = g(f(x)) \)? If so, find it.

hints.text: For part (a), substitute the entire inner function into the outer function.
\( f(g(x)) = 3x^2 - 1 \) and \( g(f(x)) = 9x^2 + 12x + 3 \). Set them equal for part (c).

problems.question_html:
A store applies a 20% discount to a price \( p \), then charges 8% sales tax on the discounted price.

(a) Write a function \( D(p) \) for the discounted price and a function \( T(p) \) for the price with tax applied.

(b) Write the composition \( (T \circ D)(p) \) that represents the final price after discount then tax. Simplify.

(c) If the original price is \$150, what is the final price? Does the order matter? Compute \( (D \circ T)(150) \) and compare.

hints.text: A 20% discount means paying 80% of the price. Sales tax of 8% means multiplying by 1.08.
\( D(p) = 0.80p \), \( T(p) = 1.08p \). \( (T \circ D)(p) = 1.08(0.80p) = 0.864p \). Both orders give the same result because multiplication is commutative.

solution_steps.text: (c) \( (T \circ D)(150) = 0.864 \times 150 = \$129.60 \). \( (D \circ T)(150) = 0.80 \times 162 = \$129.60 \). Same result because both are linear (multiplicative), and multiplication commutes.

concepts.title: Inverse Functions
concepts.content_html:
Inverse Functions

An inverse function reverses the input-output relationship of the original function. If \( f(a) = b \), then \( f^{-1}(b) = a \).

One-to-One Functions

A function has an inverse if and only if it is one-to-one (each output corresponds to exactly one input). We can test this using the horizontal line test: if every horizontal line crosses the graph at most once, the function is one-to-one.

Finding an Inverse Algebraically

To find \( f^{-1}(x) \) algebraically:

  1. Replace \( f(x) \) with \( y \): write \( y = f(x) \)
  2. Swap \( x \) and \( y \): write \( x = f(y) \)
  3. Solve for \( y \): the result is \( f^{-1}(x) \)

Domain and Range Swap

The domain of \( f \) becomes the range of \( f^{-1} \), and the range of \( f \) becomes the domain of \( f^{-1} \).

Key Idea: The graph of \( f^{-1} \) is the reflection of the graph of \( f \) across the line \( y = x \). If the point \( (a, b) \) is on the graph of \( f \), then \( (b, a) \) is on the graph of \( f^{-1} \).

Restricting the Domain

If a function is not one-to-one on its entire domain, we can restrict the domain to an interval where it is one-to-one, then find the inverse on that restricted domain. For example, \( f(x) = x^2 \) is not one-to-one on \( (-\infty, \infty) \), but it is one-to-one on \( [0, \infty) \), where \( f^{-1}(x) = \sqrt{x} \).

Worked Example

Find the inverse of \( f(x) = 3x - 7 \).

  1. Write \( y = 3x - 7 \)
  2. Swap: \( x = 3y - 7 \)
  3. Solve: \( x + 7 = 3y \), so \( y = \frac{x + 7}{3} \)

Therefore \( f^{-1}(x) = \frac{x + 7}{3} \).

Verify: \( f(f^{-1}(x)) = 3 \cdot \frac{x+7}{3} - 7 = x + 7 - 7 = x \). Confirmed.

AP Exam Tip: Remember that \( f^{-1}(x) \) does NOT mean \( \frac{1}{f(x)} \). The notation \( f^{-1} \) denotes the inverse function, not the reciprocal. Also, if \( f \) is not one-to-one, you must restrict the domain before finding the inverse.

hints.text: The inverse function reverses the input-output pair.
If \( f(5) = 12 \), then \( f^{-1}(12) = 5 \). The inverse swaps input and output.

solution_steps.text: By definition of inverse: if \( f(5) = 12 \), then \( f^{-1}(12) = 5 \).
The inverse function reverses the mapping: output becomes input, input becomes output.

problems.question_html: The function \( f(x) = 2x + 6 \) has an inverse. Which is \( f^{-1}(x) \)?

hints.text: Swap \( x \) and \( y \) in \( y = 2x + 6 \), then solve for \( y \).

solution_steps.text: Solve: \( x - 6 = 2y \), so \( y = \frac{x - 6}{2} \). Therefore \( f^{-1}(x) = \frac{x - 6}{2} \).

problems.question_html: Find \( f^{-1}(x) \) if \( f(x) = 5x + 10 \). Express in simplest form.

hints.text: Swap \( x \) and \( y \), then solve for \( y \).

problems.question_html: The function \( g(x) = x^2 \) on the domain \( (-\infty, \infty) \) does NOT have an inverse because it fails the __________ test.

hints.text: A function must be one-to-one to have an inverse. What test checks this?
The horizontal line test: if any horizontal line crosses the graph more than once, the function is not one-to-one.

solution_steps.text: The graph of \( g(x) = x^2 \) is a parabola. Horizontal lines like \( y = 4 \) cross it at two points (\( x = 2 \) and \( x = -2 \)).
This means \( g \) is not one-to-one and fails the horizontal line test, so it has no inverse on \( (-\infty, \infty) \).

problems.question_html: The function \( f(x) = \frac{x - 3}{4} \) has domain \( (-\infty, \infty) \) and range \( (-\infty, \infty) \). What are the domain and range of \( f^{-1} \)?

hints.text: The domain and range swap between a function and its inverse.
Domain of \( f \) = Range of \( f^{-1} \) = \( (-\infty, \infty) \). Range of \( f \) = Domain of \( f^{-1} \) = \( (-\infty, \infty) \).

solution_steps.text: Domain of \( f^{-1} \) = Range of \( f \) = \( (-\infty, \infty) \).
Range of \( f^{-1} \) = Domain of \( f \) = \( (-\infty, \infty) \).

problems.question_html: Which of the following functions does NOT have an inverse without restricting its domain?

hints.text: Check which function is not one-to-one. Consider the horizontal line test.
\( x^2 - 4x + 3 \) is a parabola (not one-to-one). The others are all one-to-one on their natural domains.

solution_steps.text: \( f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 3 \) is a quadratic (parabola), which fails the horizontal line test.
Linear functions, exponential functions, and square root functions are one-to-one on their domains. The quadratic requires a domain restriction.

problems.question_html: Find \( f^{-1}(x) \) if \( f(x) = \frac{2x + 1}{3} \). Express in the form \( ax + b \).

hints.text: Swap \( x \) and \( y \), then solve for \( y \).
\( x = \frac{2y + 1}{3} \). Multiply by 3: \( 3x = 2y + 1 \). Solve: \( y = \frac{3x - 1}{2} \).

solution_steps.text: Start with \( y = \frac{2x+1}{3} \). Swap: \( x = \frac{2y+1}{3} \). Multiply by 3: \( 3x = 2y + 1 \).

problems.question_html: If \( f(x) = x^2 + 1 \) with domain restricted to \( x \geq 0 \), what is the domain of \( f^{-1} \)?

hints.text: The domain of \( f^{-1} \) equals the range of \( f \). What is the range of \( f(x) = x^2 + 1 \) for \( x \geq 0 \)?
When \( x \geq 0 \), \( x^2 \geq 0 \), so \( x^2 + 1 \geq 1 \). Range of \( f \) is \( [1, \infty) \), which is the domain of \( f^{-1} \).

solution_steps.text: For \( x \geq 0 \): minimum of \( f(x) = x^2 + 1 \) is \( f(0) = 1 \), and \( f(x) \to \infty \) as \( x \to \infty \).
Range of \( f \) is \( [1, \infty) \). Domain of \( f^{-1} \) = Range of \( f \) = \( [1, \infty) \).

problems.question_html:
Let \( f(x) = \frac{4x - 5}{2} \).

(a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \).

(b) Verify your answer by showing that \( f(f^{-1}(x)) = x \) and \( f^{-1}(f(x)) = x \).

(c) State the domain and range of both \( f \) and \( f^{-1} \).

hints.text: For part (a), swap \( x \) and \( y \) and solve. For part (b), substitute one function into the other.
\( f^{-1}(x) = \frac{2x + 5}{4} \). Verify by composing: both \( f(f^{-1}(x)) \) and \( f^{-1}(f(x)) \) should simplify to \( x \).

solution_steps.text: (c) Both \( f \) and \( f^{-1} \) are linear: domain \( (-\infty, \infty) \), range \( (-\infty, \infty) \) for each.

problems.question_html:
A temperature conversion formula is \( F(C) = \frac{9}{5}C + 32 \), where \( C \) is degrees Celsius and \( F \) is degrees Fahrenheit.

(a) Find \( F^{-1}(x) \), the function that converts Fahrenheit to Celsius.

(b) What temperature in Celsius corresponds to 98.6\( ^{\circ} \)F (normal body temperature)?

(c) At what temperature are Fahrenheit and Celsius equal? Set \( F(C) = C \) and solve.

hints.text: For the inverse, swap variables and solve. Remember: the inverse converts from Fahrenheit to Celsius.
\( F^{-1}(x) = \frac{5}{9}(x - 32) \). For part (c), set \( \frac{9}{5}C + 32 = C \) and solve.

solution_steps.text: (c) \( \frac{9}{5}C + 32 = C \). \( \frac{4}{5}C = -32 \). \( C = -40 \). At \( -40^{\circ} \), Fahrenheit equals Celsius.

concepts.title: Logarithmic Expressions
concepts.content_html:
Logarithmic Expressions

A logarithm answers the question: "To what power must we raise a base to get a certain value?" Logarithms are the inverse operation of exponentiation, just as subtraction is the inverse of addition.

Definition of a Logarithm

The expression \( \log_b(c) = a \) means \( b^a = c \), where \( b > 0 \), \( b \neq 1 \), and \( c > 0 \).

In words: "the logarithm base \( b \) of \( c \) equals \( a \)" tells us that \( b \) raised to the power \( a \) produces \( c \).

Key Idea: To evaluate \( \log_b(c) \), ask yourself: "\( b \) to what power gives \( c \)?" Converting between logarithmic and exponential forms is the most fundamental skill in this unit.

Common Logarithm and Natural Logarithm

Two logarithms appear so frequently that they have special notation:

  • Common logarithm: \( \log(x) = \log_{10}(x) \). When no base is written, the base is 10.
  • Natural logarithm: \( \ln(x) = \log_e(x) \), where \( e \approx 2.718 \) is Euler's number.

Evaluating Logarithms

To evaluate a logarithm, convert to exponential form and determine the exponent.

Example 1: Evaluate \( \log_2(32) \).

Ask: \( 2^a = 32 \). Since \( 2^5 = 32 \), we have \( \log_2(32) = 5 \).

Example 2: Evaluate \( \log_3\!\left(\frac{1}{27}\right) \).

Ask: \( 3^a = \frac{1}{27} \). Since \( 3^{-3} = \frac{1}{27} \), we have \( \log_3\!\left(\frac{1}{27}\right) = -3 \).

Example 3: Evaluate \( \log(1000) \).

Ask: \( 10^a = 1000 \). Since \( 10^3 = 1000 \), we have \( \log(1000) = 3 \).

Special Logarithm Values

  • \( \log_b(1) = 0 \) for any valid base \( b \), because \( b^0 = 1 \).
  • \( \log_b(b) = 1 \) because \( b^1 = b \).
  • \( \log_b(b^n) = n \) because \( b^n = b^n \).
AP Exam Tip: Logarithms are only defined for positive arguments. The expression \( \log_b(c) \) requires \( c > 0 \). If a problem leads to \( \log \) of a negative number or zero, the expression is undefined.

problems.question_html: Which of the following is equivalent to the statement \( \log_5(125) = 3 \)?

hints.text: Recall that \( \log_b(c) = a \) means \( b^a = c \). Identify \( b \), \( a \), and \( c \).
Here \( b = 5 \), \( a = 3 \), \( c = 125 \). So the exponential form is \( 5^3 = 125 \).

solution_steps.text: The definition says \( \log_b(c) = a \) is equivalent to \( b^a = c \).
With \( b = 5 \), \( c = 125 \), and \( a = 3 \), the exponential form is \( 5^3 = 125 \).

problems.question_html: What is the value of \( \log_4(64) \)?

hints.text: Ask yourself: 4 raised to what power equals 64?

problems.question_html: Evaluate \( \log_2(16) \).

hints.text: Ask: 2 to what power equals 16?

solution_steps.text: We need the exponent \( a \) such that \( 2^a = 16 \).

problems.question_html: Evaluate \( \log(0.01) \). (Recall that \( \log \) means \( \log_{10} \).)

hints.text: Rewrite 0.01 as a power of 10.

problems.question_html: If \( \log_b(81) = 4 \), what is the value of \( b \)?

hints.text: Convert to exponential form: \( b^4 = 81 \).
Take the fourth root of 81: \( b = 81^{1/4} = 3 \) since \( 3^4 = 81 \).

problems.question_html: Which expression is equivalent to \( \ln(e^7) \)?

hints.text: Recall that \( \ln \) is the logarithm base \( e \). What does \( \log_b(b^n) \) simplify to?
\( \ln(e^7) = \log_e(e^7) = 7 \), since the logarithm and exponential are inverses.

solution_steps.text: By the identity \( \log_b(b^n) = n \), this simplifies to \( 7 \).

problems.question_html: Evaluate \( \log_9(27) \). Express your answer as a fraction.

hints.text: Try writing both 9 and 27 as powers of 3.

solution_steps.text: We need \( 9^a = 27 \). Write both in terms of base 3: \( (3^2)^a = 3^3 \).

problems.question_html: Evaluate \( \log_8\!\left(\frac{1}{64}\right) \).

hints.text: Rewrite \( \frac{1}{64} \) as a power of 8.

problems.question_html:
A scientist uses the formula \( M = \log\!\left(\frac{I}{I_0}\right) \) to measure earthquake magnitude on the Richter scale, where \( I \) is the intensity and \( I_0 \) is a reference intensity.

(a) If an earthquake has intensity \( I = 10^6 \cdot I_0 \), what is its magnitude \( M \)?

(b) Rewrite the equation \( M = \log\!\left(\frac{I}{I_0}\right) \) in exponential form, solving for \( \frac{I}{I_0} \).

(c) A magnitude-7 earthquake is how many times more intense than a magnitude-4 earthquake? Show your work.
problems.correct_answer:
(a) M = log(10^6 * I_0 / I_0) = log(10^6) = 6.
(b) 10^M = I / I_0.
(c) Magnitude 7: I_7 / I_0 = 10^7. Magnitude 4: I_4 / I_0 = 10^4. Ratio = 10^7 / 10^4 = 10^3 = 1000. A magnitude-7 earthquake is 1000 times more intense.

hints.text: For (a), substitute \( I = 10^6 \cdot I_0 \) into the formula and simplify the fraction inside the log.
For (c), find \( \frac{I}{I_0} \) for each magnitude using your answer from (b), then divide.

solution_steps.text: (c) For magnitude 7: \( \frac{I_7}{I_0} = 10^7 \). For magnitude 4: \( \frac{I_4}{I_0} = 10^4 \). The ratio is \( \frac{10^7}{10^4} = 10^3 = 1000 \).
A magnitude-7 earthquake is 1000 times more intense than a magnitude-4 earthquake.

problems.question_html:
A student claims that \( \log_2(-8) = -3 \) because \( 2^{-3} = \frac{1}{8} \), which is negative.

(a) Explain the error in the student's reasoning.

(b) Evaluate \( 2^{-3} \) and explain why it is not negative.

(c) State the values of \( x \) for which \( \log_2(x) \) is defined, and explain why.
problems.correct_answer:
(a) The student confuses a negative exponent with a negative result. The expression log_2(-8) is undefined because the argument of a logarithm must be positive.
(b) 2^(-3) = 1/2^3 = 1/8 = 0.125, which is positive, not negative.
(c) log_2(x) is defined only for x > 0 because 2 raised to any real power always produces a positive result. There is no exponent a such that 2^a is zero or negative.

hints.text: Remember: a negative exponent means a reciprocal, not a negative number. Also consider what values \( 2^a \) can produce.
\( 2^{-3} = \frac{1}{8} > 0 \). Since \( 2^a > 0 \) for all real \( a \), there is no \( a \) with \( 2^a = -8 \). So \( \log_2(-8) \) is undefined.

solution_steps.text: (a) The student incorrectly assumes a negative exponent produces a negative output. In fact, \( \log_2(-8) \) is undefined because the argument of a logarithm must be positive.
(c) \( \log_2(x) \) is defined only for \( x > 0 \) because \( 2^a > 0 \) for every real number \( a \). No exponent makes \( 2^a \) equal to zero or a negative number.

concepts.title: Inverses of Exponential Functions
concepts.content_html:
Inverses of Exponential Functions

Every exponential function \( f(x) = b^x \) (with \( b > 0 \), \( b \neq 1 \)) is one-to-one, which means it has an inverse function. That inverse is the logarithmic function \( f^{-1}(x) = \log_b(x) \).

The Inverse Relationship

If \( f(x) = b^x \), then \( f^{-1}(x) = \log_b(x) \). This means:

  • \( f(f^{-1}(x)) = b^{\log_b(x)} = x \) for all \( x > 0 \)
  • \( f^{-1}(f(x)) = \log_b(b^x) = x \) for all real \( x \)
Key Idea: The exponential function \( b^x \) and the logarithmic function \( \log_b(x) \) "undo" each other. Composing them in either order returns the original input.

Graphs as Reflections

The graph of \( y = \log_b(x) \) is the reflection of \( y = b^x \) over the line \( y = x \). This is true for all inverse function pairs.

Key observations from the reflection:

  • The point \( (0, 1) \) on \( y = b^x \) becomes \( (1, 0) \) on \( y = \log_b(x) \).
  • The point \( (1, b) \) on \( y = b^x \) becomes \( (b, 1) \) on \( y = \log_b(x) \).
  • The horizontal asymptote \( y = 0 \) of \( y = b^x \) becomes the vertical asymptote \( x = 0 \) of \( y = \log_b(x) \).

Domain and Range Swap

For inverse functions, the domain and range are exchanged:

FunctionDomainRange
\( f(x) = b^x \)All real numbers\( (0, \infty) \)
\( f^{-1}(x) = \log_b(x) \)\( (0, \infty) \)All real numbers

Worked Example

Given \( f(x) = 3^x \), find \( f^{-1}(x) \) and verify that \( f(f^{-1}(9)) = 9 \).

Step 1: The inverse of \( f(x) = 3^x \) is \( f^{-1}(x) = \log_3(x) \).

Step 2: Compute \( f^{-1}(9) = \log_3(9) = 2 \) because \( 3^2 = 9 \).

Step 3: Compute \( f(2) = 3^2 = 9 \). Confirmed: \( f(f^{-1}(9)) = 9 \).

AP Exam Tip: When a question asks you to find the inverse of an exponential function, write it in logarithmic form. Remember to swap the domain and range when describing the inverse.

hints.text: The inverse of an exponential function \( b^x \) is a logarithmic function with the same base.
The inverse of \( f(x) = 5^x \) is \( f^{-1}(x) = \log_5(x) \).

solution_steps.text: The exponential function \( f(x) = 5^x \) has base 5.
Its inverse is \( f^{-1}(x) = \log_5(x) \), the logarithm with the same base.

problems.question_html: The graph of \( y = \log_2(x) \) is a reflection of the graph of \( y = 2^x \) over which line?

hints.text: Inverse functions are always related by a specific geometric transformation.
The graph of any function and its inverse are reflections of each other over the line \( y = x \).

solution_steps.text: A function and its inverse are always reflections over the line \( y = x \).
Since \( \log_2(x) \) is the inverse of \( 2^x \), their graphs are reflections over \( y = x \).

problems.question_html:
The point \( (3, 8) \) lies on the graph of \( f(x) = 2^x \). What point must lie on the graph of \( f^{-1}(x) = \log_2(x) \)?

Enter your answer as an ordered pair, e.g., \( (a, b) \).

hints.text: For inverse functions, the coordinates of each point are swapped.

solution_steps.text: If \( (a, b) \) is on the graph of \( f \), then \( (b, a) \) is on the graph of \( f^{-1} \).

problems.question_html:
The domain of \( g(x) = \log_3(x) \) is \( (0, \infty) \). What is the range of \( g \)?

Enter: all real numbers or an interval.

hints.text: The range of a logarithmic function equals the domain of the corresponding exponential function.
The domain of \( 3^x \) is all real numbers, so the range of \( \log_3(x) \) is all real numbers.

solution_steps.text: Since \( g(x) = \log_3(x) \) is the inverse of \( h(x) = 3^x \), the range of \( g \) equals the domain of \( h \).
The domain of \( 3^x \) is all real numbers, so the range of \( \log_3(x) \) is all real numbers.

problems.question_html: What is the value of \( 10^{\log(47)} \)?

hints.text: The exponential function and logarithm with the same base are inverses. What happens when you compose them?

solution_steps.text: By the inverse property, \( b^{\log_b(x)} = x \) for all \( x > 0 \).

problems.question_html: If \( f(x) = e^x \) and \( g(x) = \ln(x) \), what is \( g(f(5)) \)?

hints.text: Think about what happens when you apply a function and then its inverse.
\( g(f(5)) = \ln(e^5) = 5 \) by the inverse property.

solution_steps.text: \( g(e^5) = \ln(e^5) = 5 \), since \( \ln \) and \( e^x \) are inverse functions.

problems.question_html: The graph of \( y = 4^x \) passes through \( (0, 1) \). What is the \( x \)-intercept of \( y = \log_4(x) \)?

hints.text: The point \( (0, 1) \) on the exponential becomes what point on the logarithm after reflecting over \( y = x \)?
Reflecting \( (0, 1) \) over \( y = x \) gives \( (1, 0) \). The \( x \)-intercept is at \( x = 1 \).

solution_steps.text: Reflect the point \( (0, 1) \) on \( y = 4^x \) over \( y = x \) to get \( (1, 0) \) on \( y = \log_4(x) \).
The \( x \)-intercept of \( y = \log_4(x) \) is at \( x = 1 \), since \( \log_4(1) = 0 \).

problems.question_html:
Given that \( f(x) = 2^{x+1} - 3 \), find \( f^{-1}(x) \).

Express your answer using \( \log_2 \).

hints.text: Set \( y = 2^{x+1} - 3 \), then solve for \( x \) in terms of \( y \).

solution_steps.text: Let \( y = 2^{x+1} - 3 \). Add 3 to both sides: \( y + 3 = 2^{x+1} \).

problems.question_html:
The function \( f(x) = 2^x \) has domain \( (-\infty, \infty) \) and range \( (0, \infty) \).

(a) State the domain and range of \( f^{-1}(x) = \log_2(x) \).

(b) The point \( (-2, \frac{1}{4}) \) is on the graph of \( f \). Identify the corresponding point on \( f^{-1} \) and verify it satisfies \( y = \log_2(x) \).

(c) Explain why \( f(x) = 2^x \) is one-to-one, and why this property guarantees the existence of an inverse.
problems.correct_answer:
(a) Domain of f^(-1): (0, infinity). Range of f^(-1): (-infinity, infinity).
(b) The corresponding point is (1/4, -2). Verify: log_2(1/4) = log_2(2^(-2)) = -2. Confirmed.
(c) f(x) = 2^x is one-to-one because it is strictly increasing: if a < b, then 2^a < 2^b. A function has an inverse if and only if it is one-to-one (passes the horizontal line test).

hints.text: For (a), remember that domain and range swap for inverse functions. For (b), swap the coordinates.
For (c), a function is one-to-one if each output corresponds to exactly one input. The horizontal line test is a graphical way to check this.

solution_steps.text: (a) Domain of \( f^{-1} \) = Range of \( f \) = \( (0, \infty) \). Range of \( f^{-1} \) = Domain of \( f \) = \( (-\infty, \infty) \).
(c) \( f(x) = 2^x \) is strictly increasing (if \( a < b \), then \( 2^a < 2^b \)), so it passes the horizontal line test. A one-to-one function always has an inverse.

problems.question_html:
A bank account balance is modeled by \( B(t) = 1000 \cdot 1.05^t \), where \( t \) is time in years.

(a) Find \( B^{-1}(x) \), the inverse function, and explain what it represents in context.

(b) Use \( B^{-1} \) to determine how many years it takes for the balance to reach \$2000. Leave your answer in terms of a logarithm.

(c) Verify your answer to (b) by showing that \( B(B^{-1}(2000)) = 2000 \).
problems.correct_answer:
(a) Set x = 1000 * 1.05^t. Divide: x/1000 = 1.05^t. Take log base 1.05: t = log_{1.05}(x/1000). B^(-1)(x) = log_{1.05}(x/1000). It represents the number of years needed for the balance to reach x dollars.
(b) B^(-1)(2000) = log_{1.05}(2000/1000) = log_{1.05}(2).
(c) B(log_{1.05}(2)) = 1000 * 1.05^{log_{1.05}(2)} = 1000 * 2 = 2000. Verified.

hints.text: To find the inverse, set \( x = 1000 \cdot 1.05^t \) and solve for \( t \).
Divide by 1000, then take \( \log_{1.05} \) of both sides. For (b), substitute \( x = 2000 \).

solution_steps.text: (a) Set \( x = 1000 \cdot 1.05^t \). Divide by 1000: \( \frac{x}{1000} = 1.05^t \). Take \( \log_{1.05} \): \( t = \log_{1.05}\!\left(\frac{x}{1000}\right) \). This gives the number of years for the balance to reach \( x \) dollars.
(c) \( B(\log_{1.05}(2)) = 1000 \cdot 1.05^{\log_{1.05}(2)} = 1000 \cdot 2 = 2000 \). Verified by the inverse property.

concepts.title: Logarithmic Functions
concepts.content_html:
Logarithmic Functions

Now that we understand logarithms as inverses of exponential functions, we study the graphs and key features of logarithmic functions in detail.

The Parent Function

The parent logarithmic function is \( f(x) = \log_b(x) \) with \( b > 0 \) and \( b \neq 1 \).

Key Features of \( f(x) = \log_b(x) \)

  • Domain: \( (0, \infty) \) — logarithms are only defined for positive inputs.
  • Range: \( (-\infty, \infty) \) — all real numbers.
  • Vertical asymptote: \( x = 0 \) (the \( y \)-axis). As \( x \to 0^+ \), \( f(x) \to -\infty \) when \( b > 1 \).
  • \( x \)-intercept: \( (1, 0) \) since \( \log_b(1) = 0 \) for any base.
  • Passes through: \( (b, 1) \) since \( \log_b(b) = 1 \).

Behavior Based on the Base

When \( b > 1 \): the function is strictly increasing. Larger inputs produce larger outputs.

When \( 0 < b < 1 \): the function is strictly decreasing. Larger inputs produce smaller outputs.

Key Idea: All logarithmic functions \( y = \log_b(x) \) pass through \( (1, 0) \) regardless of the base. This is because \( b^0 = 1 \) for every valid base.

Transformations of Logarithmic Functions

The general form \( g(x) = a \cdot \log_b(x - h) + k \) shifts and stretches the parent function:

  • \( h \) shifts the graph horizontally (and moves the vertical asymptote to \( x = h \)).
  • \( k \) shifts the graph vertically.
  • \( a \) stretches or compresses vertically (if \( a < 0 \), the graph is reflected over the \( x \)-axis).

Worked Example

Describe the graph of \( g(x) = \log_2(x - 3) + 1 \).

  • Parent function: \( \log_2(x) \)
  • Horizontal shift: Right 3 units
  • Vertical shift: Up 1 unit
  • Vertical asymptote: \( x = 3 \) (shifted from \( x = 0 \))
  • Domain: \( (3, \infty) \)
  • Key point: The point \( (1, 0) \) on the parent becomes \( (4, 1) \) on \( g \)

End Behavior

For \( f(x) = \log_b(x) \) with \( b > 1 \):

  • As \( x \to \infty \), \( f(x) \to \infty \) (increases without bound, but very slowly).
  • As \( x \to 0^+ \), \( f(x) \to -\infty \).
AP Exam Tip: When identifying transformations of \( \log \) functions, always state the new vertical asymptote and domain. A horizontal shift of \( h \) units changes both the asymptote from \( x = 0 \) to \( x = h \) and the domain from \( (0, \infty) \) to \( (h, \infty) \).

problems.question_html: What is the domain of \( f(x) = \log_3(x - 5) \)?

hints.text: The argument of a logarithm must be strictly positive. Set \( x - 5 > 0 \).
\( x - 5 > 0 \) gives \( x > 5 \), so the domain is \( (5, \infty) \).

solution_steps.text: For \( \log_3(x - 5) \) to be defined, the argument must be positive: \( x - 5 > 0 \).
Solving gives \( x > 5 \), so the domain is \( (5, \infty) \).

problems.question_html: The vertical asymptote of \( g(x) = \log_2(x + 4) \) is at which value of \( x \)?

hints.text: The vertical asymptote occurs where the argument of the logarithm equals zero.

solution_steps.text: The vertical asymptote of \( \log_b(x - h) \) is at \( x = h \). Here the argument is \( x + 4 = x - (-4) \).

problems.question_html: What is the \( x \)-intercept of \( f(x) = \log_5(x) \)?

hints.text: The \( x \)-intercept is where \( f(x) = 0 \). Set \( \log_5(x) = 0 \).

solution_steps.text: Convert to exponential form: \( 5^0 = x \), so \( x = 1 \). The \( x \)-intercept is \( (1, 0) \).

problems.question_html: Is \( f(x) = \log_{0.5}(x) \) increasing or decreasing on its domain?

hints.text: Consider whether the base is greater than 1 or between 0 and 1.
Since \( 0 < 0.5 < 1 \), the logarithmic function is strictly decreasing.

solution_steps.text: When \( 0 < b < 1 \), \( \log_b(x) \) is strictly decreasing on \( (0, \infty) \).

problems.question_html: Which of the following correctly describes the end behavior of \( f(x) = \log_3(x) \)?

choices.text: As \( x \to \infty \), \( f(x) \to \infty \); as \( x \to 0^+ \), \( f(x) \to 0 \)
As \( x \to \infty \), \( f(x) \to 3 \); as \( x \to 0^+ \), \( f(x) \to -\infty \)
As \( x \to \infty \), \( f(x) \to \infty \); as \( x \to 0^+ \), \( f(x) \to -\infty \)
As \( x \to \infty \), \( f(x) \to -\infty \); as \( x \to 0^+ \), \( f(x) \to \infty \)

hints.text: Since \( 3 > 1 \), the function is increasing. Think about what happens near the asymptote and as \( x \) grows.
Near \( x = 0 \) (from the right), \( \log_3(x) \to -\infty \). As \( x \to \infty \), \( \log_3(x) \to \infty \) (slowly).

solution_steps.text: For \( b > 1 \), \( \log_b(x) \) is increasing. As \( x \to \infty \), \( \log_3(x) \to \infty \).
As \( x \to 0^+ \), the output decreases without bound: \( \log_3(x) \to -\infty \).

problems.question_html: The function \( h(x) = -\log_2(x - 1) + 3 \) has which of the following key features?

hints.text: Identify the horizontal shift from the argument \( x - 1 \), and note the effect of the negative sign in front of \( \log_2 \).
The argument \( x - 1 > 0 \) gives domain \( (1, \infty) \) and asymptote \( x = 1 \). The negative coefficient reflects the graph, making it decreasing.

solution_steps.text: The argument is \( x - 1 \), so the asymptote is at \( x = 1 \) and the domain is \( (1, \infty) \).
The negative sign in \( -\log_2 \) reflects the graph over the \( x \)-axis, making the function decreasing.

problems.question_html: Find the \( x \)-intercept of \( g(x) = \log_2(x - 3) + 1 \). Express your answer as a decimal or fraction.

hints.text: Set \( g(x) = 0 \) and solve for \( x \).

solution_steps.text: Convert to exponential form: \( x - 3 = 2^{-1} = \frac{1}{2} \). Therefore \( x = \frac{7}{2} = 3.5 \).

problems.question_html: The range of \( f(x) = 3 + \log_4(x) \) is what interval?

hints.text: Does a vertical shift change the range of a logarithmic function?
The range of \( \log_4(x) \) is all real numbers. Adding 3 shifts every output up by 3, but the range remains all real numbers.

solution_steps.text: Adding 3 shifts the graph vertically but does not restrict the range. The range is still all real numbers.

problems.question_html:
Consider the function \( f(x) = 2\log_3(x + 1) - 4 \).

(a) State the domain, range, and vertical asymptote of \( f \).

(b) Find the \( x \)-intercept of \( f \). Show your work.

(c) Describe the end behavior of \( f \) as \( x \to \infty \) and as \( x \to -1^+ \).
problems.correct_answer:
(a) Domain: (-1, infinity). Range: all real numbers. Vertical asymptote: x = -1.
(b) Set f(x) = 0: 2*log_3(x+1) - 4 = 0, so log_3(x+1) = 2, so x+1 = 9, so x = 8. The x-intercept is (8, 0).
(c) As x -> infinity, f(x) -> infinity. As x -> -1^+, f(x) -> -infinity.

hints.text: For (a), set the argument \( x + 1 > 0 \). For (b), set \( f(x) = 0 \) and solve step by step.

solution_steps.text: (a) The argument \( x + 1 > 0 \) gives domain \( (-1, \infty) \). The vertical asymptote is \( x = -1 \). The range is all real numbers.
(c) As \( x \to \infty \), \( \log_3(x+1) \to \infty \), so \( f(x) \to \infty \). As \( x \to -1^+ \), \( \log_3(x+1) \to -\infty \), so \( f(x) \to -\infty \).

problems.question_html:
A student graphs \( f(x) = \log_2(x) \) and \( g(x) = \log_8(x) \) on the same axes.

(a) Both graphs pass through which common point? Explain why this is always true for any \( \log_b(x) \).

(b) For \( x > 1 \), which function has larger output values? Justify your answer.

(c) For \( 0 < x < 1 \), which function has larger (less negative) output values? Justify your answer.
problems.correct_answer:
(a) Both pass through (1, 0) because log_b(1) = 0 for any base b (since b^0 = 1).
(b) For x > 1, log_2(x) > log_8(x). For example, log_2(8) = 3 but log_8(8) = 1. A smaller base produces a larger exponent to reach the same value.
(c) For 0 < x < 1, both outputs are negative, but log_8(x) is less negative (closer to 0) than log_2(x). For example, log_2(1/8) = -3 while log_8(1/8) = -1.

hints.text: For (a), evaluate \( \log_b(1) \) for any base. For (b) and (c), try specific values like \( x = 8 \) and \( x = \frac{1}{8} \).
A larger base means a smaller logarithm for the same argument when \( x > 1 \). Think about it: \( 2^3 = 8 \) but \( 8^1 = 8 \).

solution_steps.text: (a) Both pass through \( (1, 0) \) because \( \log_b(1) = 0 \) for any valid base \( b \) (since \( b^0 = 1 \)).
(b) For \( x > 1 \), \( \log_2(x) > \log_8(x) \). Example: \( \log_2(8) = 3 \) while \( \log_8(8) = 1 \). A smaller base requires a larger exponent.
(c) For \( 0 < x < 1 \), both outputs are negative. \( \log_8(x) \) is closer to 0 (less negative). Example: \( \log_2(\frac{1}{8}) = -3 \) while \( \log_8(\frac{1}{8}) = -1 \).

concepts.title: Logarithmic Function Manipulation
concepts.content_html:
Logarithmic Function Manipulation

Logarithmic properties allow us to rewrite complex expressions in simpler forms. These properties follow directly from the exponent rules, since logarithms are exponents.

The Three Core Properties

Product Rule: \( \log_b(MN) = \log_b(M) + \log_b(N) \)

The logarithm of a product equals the sum of the logarithms.

Quotient Rule: \( \log_b\!\left(\frac{M}{N}\right) = \log_b(M) - \log_b(N) \)

The logarithm of a quotient equals the difference of the logarithms.

Power Rule: \( \log_b(M^p) = p \cdot \log_b(M) \)

The logarithm of a power equals the exponent times the logarithm.

Key Idea: These three rules come from the corresponding exponent rules: \( b^m \cdot b^n = b^{m+n} \) gives the product rule, \( \frac{b^m}{b^n} = b^{m-n} \) gives the quotient rule, and \( (b^m)^p = b^{mp} \) gives the power rule.

Change of Base Formula

To evaluate a logarithm in any base using a calculator (which only has \( \log \) and \( \ln \)):

\[ \log_b(x) = \frac{\log(x)}{\log(b)} = \frac{\ln(x)}{\ln(b)} \]

Expanding Logarithmic Expressions

Example: Expand \( \log_2\!\left(\frac{x^3 y}{z^2}\right) \).

\[ \log_2\!\left(\frac{x^3 y}{z^2}\right) = \log_2(x^3 y) - \log_2(z^2) = \log_2(x^3) + \log_2(y) - \log_2(z^2) = 3\log_2(x) + \log_2(y) - 2\log_2(z) \]

Condensing Logarithmic Expressions

Example: Condense \( 2\ln(x) - \ln(y) + \ln(3) \).

\[ 2\ln(x) - \ln(y) + \ln(3) = \ln(x^2) - \ln(y) + \ln(3) = \ln\!\left(\frac{3x^2}{y}\right) \]

AP Exam Tip: There is no logarithm rule for \( \log_b(M + N) \). This is a very common mistake: \( \log_b(M + N) \neq \log_b(M) + \log_b(N) \). The product rule applies to \( \log_b(M \cdot N) \), not \( \log_b(M + N) \).

problems.question_html: Which expression is equivalent to \( \log_3(12) \)?

hints.text: Factor 12 as a product and apply the product rule.
\( 12 = 4 \times 3 \), so \( \log_3(12) = \log_3(4) + \log_3(3) \) by the product rule.

problems.question_html: Which expression equals \( \log_5(x^4) \)?

hints.text: Which log property deals with exponents inside the argument?
The power rule states \( \log_b(M^p) = p \cdot \log_b(M) \). So \( \log_5(x^4) = 4\log_5(x) \).

problems.question_html: Expand: \( \log_2\!\left(\frac{a}{b}\right) \). Write your answer in the form \( \log_2(a) \text{ [operation] } \log_2(b) \).

hints.text: The quotient rule converts a log of a fraction into a difference.
\( \log_2\!\left(\frac{a}{b}\right) = \log_2(a) - \log_2(b) \).

problems.question_html: Use the change of base formula to rewrite \( \log_7(50) \) using common logarithms. Write your answer as a fraction of two \( \log \) expressions.

hints.text: The change of base formula says \( \log_b(x) = \frac{\log(x)}{\log(b)} \).

solution_steps.text: Apply the change of base formula: \( \log_b(x) = \frac{\log(x)}{\log(b)} \).

problems.question_html: Expand completely: \( \ln\!\left(\frac{x^2\sqrt{y}}{z^3}\right) \)

hints.text: Apply quotient rule first, then product rule on the numerator, then power rule on each term.

problems.question_html: Condense into a single logarithm: \( 3\log(x) + \log(y) - 2\log(z) \).

hints.text: First apply the power rule to move coefficients inside as exponents, then combine using product and quotient rules.
\( \log(x^3) + \log(y) - \log(z^2) = \log\!\left(\frac{x^3 y}{z^2}\right) \).

problems.question_html: Condense: \( \frac{1}{3}\log_2(27) + \log_2(4) \). Evaluate the result as a single number.

hints.text: Use the power rule on \( \frac{1}{3}\log_2(27) \) first, then combine with the product rule.

problems.question_html: If \( \log(2) \approx 0.301 \) and \( \log(3) \approx 0.477 \), find \( \log(72) \). Round to three decimal places.

hints.text: Factor 72 into primes: \( 72 = 8 \times 9 = 2^3 \times 3^2 \).

problems.question_html:
Given that \( \log_4(x) = 2.5 \):

(a) Find the exact value of \( x \).

(b) Use the change of base formula to express \( \log_4(x) \) using natural logarithms, and verify that \( \frac{\ln(x)}{\ln(4)} = 2.5 \).

(c) Use log properties to find \( \log_4(16x^2) \).

hints.text: For (a), convert to exponential form: \( 4^{2.5} = x \). For (c), use the product and power rules.

problems.question_html:
A student writes: \( \log_2(x + y) = \log_2(x) + \log_2(y) \).

(a) Show that this equation is false by choosing specific positive values of \( x \) and \( y \) and evaluating both sides.

(b) State the correct property the student is confusing this with, and write it correctly.

(c) Expand \( \log_2(x^2(x+1)) \) completely. Explain which parts can be simplified further and which cannot.
problems.correct_answer:
(a) Let x = 2 and y = 2. Left side: log_2(2+2) = log_2(4) = 2. Right side: log_2(2) + log_2(2) = 1 + 1 = 2. These happen to be equal! Try x = 1 and y = 3. Left: log_2(4) = 2. Right: log_2(1) + log_2(3) = 0 + log_2(3) ≈ 1.585. Since 2 ≠ 1.585, the equation is false.
(b) The student is confusing log_2(x + y) with log_2(x * y). The correct product rule is: log_2(x * y) = log_2(x) + log_2(y).
(c) log_2(x^2(x+1)) = log_2(x^2) + log_2(x+1) = 2*log_2(x) + log_2(x+1). The term 2*log_2(x) uses the power rule. The term log_2(x+1) cannot be simplified further because there is no log rule for sums inside a logarithm.

hints.text: For (a), try \( x = 1 \) and \( y = 3 \) and compare \( \log_2(4) \) to \( \log_2(1) + \log_2(3) \).
The product rule says \( \log_b(M \cdot N) = \log_b(M) + \log_b(N) \), not \( \log_b(M + N) \). There is no rule for the log of a sum.

solution_steps.text: (a) Let \( x = 1 \), \( y = 3 \). Left: \( \log_2(1 + 3) = \log_2(4) = 2 \). Right: \( \log_2(1) + \log_2(3) = 0 + \log_2(3) \approx 1.585 \). Since \( 2 \neq 1.585 \), the statement is false.
(b) The correct property is the product rule: \( \log_2(x \cdot y) = \log_2(x) + \log_2(y) \). The student applied it to a sum, not a product.
(c) \( \log_2(x^2(x+1)) = \log_2(x^2) + \log_2(x+1) = 2\log_2(x) + \log_2(x+1) \). The term \( \log_2(x+1) \) cannot be simplified further because there is no rule for a log of a sum.

concepts.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Equations and Inequalities
concepts.content_html:
Exponential and Logarithmic Equations and Inequalities

Many real-world problems require solving equations where the variable appears in an exponent or inside a logarithm. The key strategy is to use the inverse relationship between exponentials and logarithms.

Solving Exponential Equations

Strategy: Isolate the exponential expression, then take the logarithm of both sides.

Example: Solve \( 3 \cdot 2^x = 48 \).

  1. Divide both sides by 3: \( 2^x = 16 \).
  2. Take \( \log_2 \) of both sides: \( x = \log_2(16) = 4 \).

Example: Solve \( 5^{2x-1} = 20 \).

  1. Take \( \ln \) of both sides: \( (2x - 1)\ln(5) = \ln(20) \).
  2. Solve for \( x \): \( x = \frac{\ln(20)/\ln(5) + 1}{2} = \frac{\log_5(20) + 1}{2} \).

Solving Logarithmic Equations

Strategy: Isolate the logarithm (or condense multiple logarithms into one), then convert to exponential form.

Example: Solve \( \log_3(x - 2) = 4 \).

  1. Convert to exponential form: \( x - 2 = 3^4 = 81 \).
  2. Solve: \( x = 83 \).
  3. Check: \( x - 2 = 81 > 0 \). Valid.
Key Idea: Always check solutions to logarithmic equations. A solution is extraneous if it makes the argument of any logarithm zero or negative. Plug your answer back into the original equation to verify.

Extraneous Solutions

Example: Solve \( \log_2(x) + \log_2(x - 2) = 3 \).

  1. Condense: \( \log_2(x(x-2)) = 3 \).
  2. Exponential form: \( x(x - 2) = 8 \), so \( x^2 - 2x - 8 = 0 \).
  3. Factor: \( (x - 4)(x + 2) = 0 \), giving \( x = 4 \) or \( x = -2 \).
  4. Check \( x = -2 \): \( \log_2(-2) \) is undefined. Reject.
  5. Check \( x = 4 \): \( \log_2(4) + \log_2(2) = 2 + 1 = 3 \). Valid.

Exponential and Logarithmic Inequalities

The same strategies apply, but you must consider the direction of the inequality based on whether the function is increasing or decreasing.

For \( b > 1 \): \( \log_b(x) > a \) implies \( x > b^a \), and \( b^x > c \) implies \( x > \log_b(c) \).

For \( 0 < b < 1 \): the inequalities flip because the function is decreasing.

AP Exam Tip: On the AP exam, always show your check for extraneous solutions. Simply stating "no extraneous solutions" without verification may not earn full credit.

(b) Solve the resulting quadratic equation.

problems.correct_answer:
(a) log_3((x+6)(x-2)) = 2, so (x+6)(x-2) = 3^2 = 9.
(b) x^2 + 4x - 12 = 9, so x^2 + 4x - 21 = 0. Factor: (x+7)(x-3) = 0. x = -7 or x = 3.
(c) Check x = -7: log_3(-7+6) = log_3(-1), undefined. Reject. Check x = 3: log_3(9) + log_3(1) = 2 + 0 = 2. Valid. The only solution is x = 3.

hints.text: Use the product rule to condense, then convert \( \log_3(\text{expression}) = 2 \) to exponential form.
After converting, you get \( (x+6)(x-2) = 9 \). Expand, set equal to 0, and factor. Don't forget to check both solutions.

solution_steps.text: (c) Check \( x = -7 \): \( \log_3(-1) \) is undefined. Extraneous. Check \( x = 3 \): \( \log_3(9) + \log_3(1) = 2 + 0 = 2 \). Valid. The only solution is \( x = 3 \).

concepts.title: Logarithmic Function Context and Data Modeling
concepts.content_html:
Logarithmic Function Context and Data Modeling

Logarithmic functions model situations where growth is rapid initially and then slows dramatically. Many real-world phenomena exhibit this pattern, making logarithmic models valuable tools in science and social science.

When to Use a Logarithmic Model

A logarithmic model \( f(x) = a + b\ln(x) \) (or \( f(x) = a + b\log(x) \)) is appropriate when:

  • Data increases (or decreases) rapidly at first, then levels off.
  • There is no maximum value, but the rate of increase continually slows.
  • A scatterplot of \( y \) vs. \( \ln(x) \) (or \( \log(x) \)) appears linear.

Real-World Examples

  • Decibel scale: Sound intensity measured in decibels uses \( \log \).
  • Richter scale: Earthquake magnitude is logarithmic.
  • pH scale: Acidity is \( \text{pH} = -\log[H^+] \).
  • Learning curves: Performance improves quickly, then plateaus.

Logarithmic Regression

Given a data set, a calculator can perform logarithmic regression (LnReg) to find the best-fitting model of the form \( y = a + b\ln(x) \). The process:

  1. Enter data into lists on your calculator.
  2. Run LnReg (or similar command).
  3. The calculator returns the values of \( a \) and \( b \) that best fit the data.

Worked Example

A researcher records the number of species \( S \) found in a forest as the area \( A \) (in hectares) increases:

Area \( A \)Species \( S \)
15
1015
10025
100035

Notice the pattern: each time the area increases by a factor of 10, the number of species increases by approximately 10. This suggests a logarithmic model \( S = a + b\log(A) \).

Using the data: when \( A = 1 \), \( S = 5 \), so \( a = 5 \). When \( A = 10 \), \( S = 15 \), so \( 5 + b\log(10) = 15 \), giving \( b = 10 \). The model is \( S = 5 + 10\log(A) \).

Key Idea: In the model \( f(x) = a + b\log_n(x) \), the constant \( a \) represents the output when \( x = 1 \) (since \( \log_n(1) = 0 \)), and \( b \) controls how rapidly the function grows.
AP Exam Tip: On the AP Precalculus exam, you are NOT expected to interpret the contextual meaning of \( a \) and \( b \) in \( f(x) = a + b\log_n(x) \). Focus instead on using the model to make predictions and on understanding when a logarithmic model is appropriate.

problems.correct_answer:
(a) ln(1)=0, ln(5)≈1.61, ln(25)≈3.22, ln(125)≈4.83, ln(625)≈6.44. Plotting S vs ln(A) gives approximately equal spacing in both variables, suggesting a linear relationship between S and ln(A), which supports a logarithmic model.
(b) When A=1: 10 = a + b*ln(1) = a + 0, so a = 10. When A=25: 30 = 10 + b*ln(25). So b = 20/ln(25) ≈ 20/3.219 ≈ 6.21. Model: S = 10 + 6.21*ln(A).
(c) S = 10 + 6.21*ln(50) = 10 + 6.21*3.912 ≈ 10 + 24.3 ≈ 34. The model predicts approximately 34 species.

solution_steps.text: (a) \( \ln(1) = 0 \), \( \ln(5) \approx 1.61 \), \( \ln(25) \approx 3.22 \), \( \ln(125) \approx 4.83 \), \( \ln(625) \approx 6.44 \). The \( \ln(A) \) values increase by about 1.61 each time, and \( S \) increases by 10 each time. The linear pattern in \( S \) vs. \( \ln(A) \) supports a logarithmic model.

problems.question_html:
Two students debate which model best fits the data showing website traffic \( y \) (in thousands of visits) versus months since launch \( x \):

\( x \)124816
\( y \)2581114

Student A suggests an exponential model. Student B suggests a logarithmic model.

(a) Explain why the data pattern supports Student B's claim over Student A's.

(b) Using the model \( y = a + b\ln(x) \), find \( a \) and \( b \) using the points \( (1, 2) \) and \( (16, 14) \).

(c) According to the model, when will traffic reach 20,000 visits? Show your work.
problems.correct_answer:
(a) The data increases quickly at first (2 to 5 to 8) then slows (8 to 11 to 14), with diminishing returns. An exponential model would show accelerating growth, not decelerating. The logarithmic pattern of rapid initial growth that slows is a better fit.
(b) At x=1: 2 = a + b*ln(1) = a, so a = 2. At x=16: 14 = 2 + b*ln(16). b = 12/ln(16) = 12/(4*ln(2)) = 3/ln(2) ≈ 4.328. Model: y = 2 + 4.328*ln(x).
(c) Set 20 = 2 + 4.328*ln(x). 18 = 4.328*ln(x). ln(x) = 18/4.328 ≈ 4.159. x = e^4.159 ≈ 64. Traffic will reach 20,000 visits after approximately 64 months.

hints.text: For (a), compare how the differences between consecutive \( y \)-values change. Are they increasing (exponential) or decreasing (logarithmic)?
For (b), use \( x = 1 \) first since \( \ln(1) = 0 \). For (c), set \( y = 20 \) and solve for \( x \).

solution_steps.text: (a) The differences between consecutive \( y \)-values are 3, 3, 3, 3 for doubling \( x \)-values. The growth rate is decreasing relative to \( x \), consistent with logarithmic (not exponential) behavior.

concepts.title: Semi-log Plots
concepts.content_html:
Semi-log Plots

A semi-log plot (also called a semi-logarithmic plot) uses a logarithmic scale on the \( y \)-axis and a linear scale on the \( x \)-axis. This type of plot is specifically designed to reveal exponential relationships in data.

Why Use Semi-log Plots?

When data follows an exponential model \( y = ab^x \), a standard plot can make it hard to see the pattern, especially when \( y \)-values span many orders of magnitude. A semi-log plot transforms the exponential curve into a straight line, making the relationship easier to identify and analyze.

The Mathematics Behind Semi-log Plots

Start with an exponential function: \( y = ab^x \).

Take the logarithm of both sides:

\[ \log(y) = \log(ab^x) = \log(a) + x\log(b) \]

Let \( Y = \log(y) \). Then:

\[ Y = \log(b) \cdot x + \log(a) \]

This is a linear equation in \( x \) and \( Y \), with slope \( \log(b) \) and \( Y \)-intercept \( \log(a) \).

Key Idea: If data is exponential (\( y = ab^x \)), then a semi-log plot (\( \log(y) \) vs. \( x \)) produces a straight line. The slope of that line is \( \log(b) \) and the \( y \)-intercept is \( \log(a) \).

Reading a Semi-log Plot

On a semi-log plot:

  • The \( y \)-axis is labeled with powers of 10 (or equally spaced logarithmic values): 1, 10, 100, 1000, ...
  • The \( x \)-axis is labeled with regular, equally spaced values.
  • A straight line on this plot means the data is exponential.
  • A curve on this plot means the data is NOT exponential.

Worked Example

A bacteria population is measured over time:

\( t \) (hours)01234
\( P \)1002004008001600

Compute \( \log(P) \) for each value:

\( t \)01234
\( \log(P) \)22.3012.6022.9033.204

The \( \log(P) \) values increase by approximately 0.301 for each unit increase in \( t \). This constant difference confirms the data is exponential.

The slope is \( 0.301 = \log(2) \), so \( b = 2 \). The intercept is \( \log(a) = 2 \), so \( a = 100 \). The model is \( P = 100 \cdot 2^t \).

AP Exam Tip: On the AP Precalculus exam, semi-log plots use a logarithmic scale on the \( y \)-axis only (not the \( x \)-axis). A plot with logarithmic scaling on both axes is called a log-log plot and is NOT part of this course. If data appears linear on a semi-log plot, the original data is exponential.

If \( y = ab^x \), then \( \log(y) = \log(a) + x\log(b) \), which is linear in \( x \).

solution_steps.text: A semi-log plot graphs \( \log(y) \) vs. \( x \). If \( y = ab^x \), then \( \log(y) = \log(a) + x\log(b) \).
This is a linear equation, so the data appears as a straight line.

By convention (and per the AP CED), the \( y \)-axis uses the logarithmic scale.

\( \log(y) = \log(50) + x\log(3) \). The slope is \( \log(3) \).

problems.question_html: The \( y \)-intercept of a line on a semi-log plot is 3 (meaning \( \log(y) = 3 \) when \( x = 0 \)). What is the value of \( a \) in the exponential model \( y = a \cdot b^x \)?
A semi-log plot of data shows a straight line with slope 0.477 and \( y \)-intercept 2. Which exponential model fits the data?

solution_steps.text: From the slope: \( \log(b) = 0.477 \), so \( b = 10^{0.477} \approx 3 \). The model is \( y = 100 \cdot 3^x \).

solution_steps.text: Exponential data produces a straight line on a semi-log plot.
A curve on a semi-log plot means the data is NOT exponential.

problems.question_html: An exponential model is \( y = 200 \cdot 5^x \). On a semi-log plot, what is the value of \( \log(y) \) when \( x = 3 \)?

\( \log(y) = \log(200) + 3\log(5) \). Since \( \log(200) = \log(2 \cdot 100) = \log(2) + 2 \approx 2.301 \), and \( \log(5) \approx 0.699 \), we get approximately \( 2.301 + 2.097 = 4.398 \). In exact form: \( \log(200) + 3\log(5) \).
