problems.question_html:
Two data sets are each plotted on a semi-log plot. Data Set A appears as a straight line with positive slope. Data Set B appears as a straight line with negative slope.

(a) What type of model fits Data Set A? Write the general form and explain why the slope is positive.

(b) What type of model fits Data Set B? Write the general form and explain why the slope is negative.

(c) A third data set, plotted on the same semi-log axes, appears as a horizontal line. What does this imply about the data? Write the corresponding model.
problems.correct_answer:
(a) Data Set A fits an exponential growth model y = a*b^x with b > 1. The slope is log(b) > 0 because b > 1 means log(b) is positive.
(b) Data Set B fits an exponential decay model y = a*b^x with 0 < b < 1. The slope is log(b) < 0 because 0 < b < 1 means log(b) is negative.
(c) A horizontal line means slope = 0, so log(b) = 0, meaning b = 1. The model is y = a*1^x = a, a constant function. The data has no growth or decay.

hints.text: Remember that the slope of the semi-log line equals \( \log(b) \). What values of \( b \) make \( \log(b) \) positive, negative, or zero?
Positive slope: \( b > 1 \) (growth). Negative slope: \( 0 < b < 1 \) (decay). Zero slope: \( b = 1 \) (constant).

solution_steps.text: (a) Exponential growth: \( y = ab^x \) with \( b > 1 \). The slope \( \log(b) > 0 \) because \( b > 1 \).
(b) Exponential decay: \( y = ab^x \) with \( 0 < b < 1 \). The slope \( \log(b) < 0 \) because \( 0 < b < 1 \).
(c) Horizontal line: slope = 0, so \( \log(b) = 0 \) and \( b = 1 \). Model: \( y = a \), a constant function with no growth or decay.

topics.name: Unit 3: Trigonometric and Polar Functions
topics.description: Master trigonometric functions, identities, inverse trig, equations, polar coordinates, polar function graphs, and rates of change in polar functions. This unit covers 30-35% of the AP Precalculus Exam.

concepts.title: Periodic Phenomena
concepts.content_html:
Periodic Phenomena

Many real-world quantities repeat in predictable patterns: the height of a point on a spinning wheel, the tides in a harbor, or the average monthly temperature in a city. These repeating patterns are called periodic phenomena.

What Makes a Function Periodic?

A function \( f \) is periodic if there exists a positive constant \( k \) such that \( f(x + k) = f(x) \) for all \( x \) in the domain of \( f \). The smallest such positive value \( k \) is called the period of the function.

Key Idea: The period is the smallest horizontal distance after which the function's values begin to repeat. One complete cycle of the function spans exactly one period.

Identifying Periodic Behavior

To determine whether a function is periodic from a graph or table:

  • Look for a repeating pattern in the output values.
  • Measure the horizontal distance between identical points on consecutive cycles (e.g., two consecutive peaks or two consecutive troughs).
  • Verify that the pattern repeats consistently.

Constructing a Graph from One Cycle

If you know one complete cycle of a periodic function, you can construct the entire graph by repeating that cycle to the left and right. Each copy is shifted horizontally by the period \( k \).

Worked Example

A data set records the depth of water in a tidal pool every hour. The depths (in feet) repeat every 12 hours:

Hour03691215
Depth2.55.02.50.02.55.0

Since the depth at hour 12 equals the depth at hour 0, and the depth at hour 15 equals the depth at hour 3, the function is periodic with period \( k = 12 \) hours.

Estimating the Period

When data is not perfectly periodic (due to measurement noise), estimate the period by finding the average horizontal distance between successive peaks (maximums) or successive troughs (minimums).

AP Exam Tip: When asked to identify the period from a graph, measure the distance between two corresponding points on consecutive cycles (peak to peak or trough to trough), not from the start of the graph to the first peak.

problems.question_html: A function \( f \) is periodic with period 5. If \( f(2) = 7 \), what is \( f(17) \)?

hints.text: A periodic function repeats its values every period. How many periods fit between 2 and 17?

solution_steps.text: Since \( f \) has period 5, we know \( f(x + 5) = f(x) \) for all \( x \).

problems.question_html: The graph of a periodic function shows peaks at \( x = 3 \), \( x = 11 \), and \( x = 19 \). What is the period of the function?

hints.text: The period is the horizontal distance between consecutive peaks.
Distance between consecutive peaks: \( 11 - 3 = 8 \). Verify: \( 19 - 11 = 8 \). The period is 8.

solution_steps.text: The period equals the distance between consecutive corresponding points (peak to peak).

problems.question_html: A periodic function has period 6. If the function completes one full cycle starting at \( x = 0 \), at what \( x \)-value does the third complete cycle end?

hints.text: Each cycle spans one full period. After how many periods does the third cycle end?
Three complete cycles: \( 3 \times 6 = 18 \).

solution_steps.text: One cycle spans a distance equal to the period: 6 units.
Three complete cycles end at \( x = 3 \times 6 = 18 \).

problems.question_html: A function \( g \) is periodic with period 10. If \( g(4) = -3 \), then \( g(24) = \) ________.

hints.text: How many full periods separate \( x = 4 \) from \( x = 24 \)?

solution_steps.text: Since the period is 10, \( g(x + 10) = g(x) \) for all \( x \).

problems.question_html: A periodic function \( f \) has values \( f(0) = 1 \), \( f(3) = 4 \), \( f(6) = 1 \), \( f(9) = 4 \), and \( f(12) = 1 \). Which of the following could be the period of \( f \)?

hints.text: Look for the smallest shift after which all values repeat. Does the pattern \( 1, 4 \) repeat every 3 units? Every 6 units?
If the period were 3, then \( f(0) \) would equal \( f(3) \), but \( 1 \neq 4 \). With period 6: \( f(0) = f(6) = f(12) = 1 \) and \( f(3) = f(9) = 4 \). Period 6 works.

solution_steps.text: Test period 3: \( f(0) = 1 \) but \( f(3) = 4 \), so \( f(0) \neq f(3) \). Period 3 fails.
Test period 6: \( f(0) = f(6) = f(12) = 1 \) and \( f(3) = f(9) = 4 \). All values match, so the period could be 6.
Period 9 fails because \( f(0) = 1 \) but \( f(9) = 4 \). Period 12 is possible but not the smallest. The answer is 6.

problems.question_html: The temperature in a greenhouse cycles between \( 65^\circ\text{F} \) and \( 85^\circ\text{F} \) every 24 hours. A sensor records the temperature reaching \( 85^\circ\text{F} \) at \( t = 6 \) hours and again at \( t = 30 \) hours. Which of the following best describes the period?

hints.text: The period is the distance between consecutive identical points in the cycle. The maximum occurs at \( t = 6 \) and the next maximum at \( t = 30 \).
\( 30 - 6 = 24 \) hours between consecutive maximums. The period is 24 hours.

solution_steps.text: The maximum temperature \( 85^\circ\text{F} \) occurs at \( t = 6 \) and next at \( t = 30 \).
The period is the time between consecutive maximums: \( 30 - 6 = 24 \) hours.

problems.question_html: A periodic function \( h \) has period 7. If \( h(5) = 12 \), find the value of \( h(40) + h(47) \).

hints.text: Reduce both 40 and 47 modulo 7 to find equivalent inputs within one period.

problems.question_html: A periodic function \( f \) satisfies \( f(x + k) = f(x) \) for all \( x \). The smallest such positive \( k \) is called the __________ of the function.

hints.text: This is the fundamental vocabulary term for the smallest repeating interval of a periodic function.
The smallest positive \( k \) for which \( f(x+k) = f(x) \) is called the period.

solution_steps.text: By definition, a periodic function repeats its values every \( k \) units.
The smallest such positive \( k \) is called the period of the function.

problems.question_html:
A Ferris wheel completes one revolution every 40 seconds. A rider boards at the bottom of the wheel, which is 2 meters above the ground. The top of the wheel is 18 meters above the ground.

(a) What is the period of the rider's height as a function of time?

(b) Describe the rider's height at \( t = 0 \), \( t = 10 \), \( t = 20 \), and \( t = 30 \) seconds.

(c) At what time(s) during the first two revolutions does the rider return to their starting height of 2 meters?
problems.correct_answer:
(a) The period is 40 seconds (one full revolution).
(b) At t = 0, the rider is at the bottom: 2 m. At t = 10 (quarter revolution), the rider is at the midpoint: 10 m. At t = 20 (half revolution), the rider is at the top: 18 m. At t = 30 (three-quarter revolution), the rider is back at the midpoint: 10 m.
(c) The rider returns to 2 m at the end of each full revolution: t = 40 s and t = 80 s.

hints.text: The period equals the time for one complete revolution. Think about what fraction of the revolution corresponds to each time value.

The wheel diameter is \( 18 - 2 = 16 \) m, so the radius is 8 m and the center is at 10 m. At quarter-period intervals, the rider alternates between bottom (2 m), middle (10 m), top (18 m), and middle (10 m).

solution_steps.text: (a) The Ferris wheel completes one revolution in 40 seconds, so the period is 40 seconds.

(b) The wheel has radius \( \frac{18 - 2}{2} = 8 \) m and center height \( 2 + 8 = 10 \) m. At \( t = 0 \): bottom = 2 m. At \( t = 10 \): quarter turn = 10 m. At \( t = 20 \): half turn = 18 m. At \( t = 30 \): three-quarter turn = 10 m.
(c) The rider returns to 2 m (the bottom) after each complete revolution: at \( t = 40 \) s and \( t = 80 \) s during the first two revolutions.

problems.question_html:
The table below shows the average monthly high temperature (in \( ^\circ\text{F} \)) for a city over two years.

Month1234567891011121314
Temp4044556575859088806855424044

(a) Explain why this data suggests a periodic function. What is the estimated period?

(b) Estimate the maximum and minimum temperatures and the months in which they occur.

(c) If this periodic pattern continues, predict the temperature in month 19.
problems.correct_answer:
(a) The data suggests a periodic function because the temperature values in months 13 and 14 match months 1 and 2 respectively. The estimated period is 12 months.
(b) Maximum temperature is approximately 90°F in month 7. Minimum temperature is approximately 40°F in month 1 (and month 13).
(c) Month 19 corresponds to month 19 - 12 = 7, so the predicted temperature is approximately 90°F.

hints.text: Compare the temperatures in months 1 and 13, and months 2 and 14. What pattern do you see?
Since the values repeat after 12 months, the period is 12. To predict month 19, find \( 19 \mod 12 = 7 \) and look up the temperature for month 7.

solution_steps.text: (a) The temperature at month 13 equals month 1 (both 40) and month 14 equals month 2 (both 44). This repeating pattern with a shift of 12 indicates a periodic function with period 12 months.
(b) Scanning the data: the maximum is \( 90^\circ\text{F} \) in month 7, and the minimum is \( 40^\circ\text{F} \) in month 1.
(c) \( 19 - 12 = 7 \), so month 19 corresponds to month 7. The predicted temperature is \( 90^\circ\text{F} \).

concepts.title: Sine, Cosine, and Tangent
concepts.content_html:
Sine, Cosine, and Tangent

The trigonometric functions sine, cosine, and tangent are defined using the unit circle, a circle of radius 1 centered at the origin.

Radian Measure

An angle measured in radians corresponds to the length of the arc on the unit circle subtended by that angle. One full revolution equals \( 2\pi \) radians. The relationship between arc length \( s \), radius \( r \), and angle \( \theta \) (in radians) is:

\[ s = r\theta \]

For the unit circle (\( r = 1 \)), the arc length equals the angle measure in radians: \( s = \theta \).

Key Idea: The word "subtended" describes the angle that corresponds to a given arc, not the arc itself. An angle is subtended by an arc; equivalently, an arc is intercepted by an angle.

Unit Circle Definitions

Let \( P(x, y) \) be the point on the unit circle corresponding to angle \( \theta \) measured from the positive \( x \)-axis. Then:

\[ \cos(\theta) = x, \quad \sin(\theta) = y, \quad \tan(\theta) = \frac{y}{x} = \frac{\sin(\theta)}{\cos(\theta)} \]

The cosine gives the horizontal coordinate, and the sine gives the vertical coordinate of the point on the unit circle.

Signs by Quadrant

The signs of sine, cosine, and tangent depend on which quadrant the terminal side of the angle lies in:

  • Quadrant I (\( 0 < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2} \)): all positive
  • Quadrant II (\( \frac{\pi}{2} < \theta < \pi \)): sine positive, cosine and tangent negative
  • Quadrant III (\( \pi < \theta < \frac{3\pi}{2} \)): tangent positive, sine and cosine negative
  • Quadrant IV (\( \frac{3\pi}{2} < \theta < 2\pi \)): cosine positive, sine and tangent negative

A common mnemonic is "All Students Take Calculus" (A-S-T-C), indicating which functions are positive in Quadrants I through IV.

Worked Example

Find the arc length of a sector with radius \( r = 5 \) cm and central angle \( \theta = \frac{\pi}{3} \) radians.

Using \( s = r\theta \):

\[ s = 5 \cdot \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{5\pi}{3} \approx 5.24 \text{ cm} \]
AP Exam Tip: The AP Precalculus exam uses radians exclusively. Make sure your calculator is in radian mode, and be comfortable converting between degrees and radians: \( \theta_{\text{rad}} = \theta_{\text{deg}} \cdot \frac{\pi}{180} \).

problems.question_html: On the unit circle, the angle \( \theta = \frac{\pi}{2} \) corresponds to which point?

hints.text: Starting from \( (1, 0) \), an angle of \( \frac{\pi}{2} \) radians is a quarter turn counterclockwise.
A quarter turn counterclockwise from \( (1, 0) \) lands at the top of the circle: \( (0, 1) \).

solution_steps.text: The angle \( \frac{\pi}{2} \) radians equals \( 90^\circ \), which is a quarter revolution counterclockwise.
Starting from \( (1, 0) \), this reaches the point \( (0, 1) \) at the top of the unit circle.

problems.question_html: An angle \( \theta \) is in Quadrant III. Which of the following is true about \( \sin(\theta) \) and \( \cos(\theta) \)?

hints.text: In Quadrant III, both the \( x \)- and \( y \)-coordinates are negative.
Since \( \cos(\theta) = x \) and \( \sin(\theta) = y \), both are negative in Quadrant III.

solution_steps.text: In Quadrant III, the terminal point \( P(x, y) \) has \( x < 0 \) and \( y < 0 \).
Since \( \cos(\theta) = x \) and \( \sin(\theta) = y \), both sine and cosine are negative.

problems.question_html: A circle has radius \( r = 10 \) cm. Find the arc length subtended by a central angle of \( \frac{\pi}{4} \) radians.

hints.text: Use the arc length formula \( s = r\theta \).

solution_steps.text: Apply the formula \( s = r\theta \) with \( r = 10 \) and \( \theta = \frac{\pi}{4} \).

problems.question_html: Convert \( 270^\circ \) to radians. Express your answer as a fraction involving \( \pi \).

hints.text: Multiply the degree measure by \( \frac{\pi}{180} \).

problems.question_html: The point \( P \) on the unit circle corresponds to angle \( \theta \) and has coordinates \( \left( -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\, \frac{1}{2} \right) \). What is \( \tan(\theta) \)?

hints.text: Recall that \( \tan(\theta) = \frac{y}{x} \) where \( (x, y) \) is the point on the unit circle.

problems.question_html: A wheel with radius 30 cm rotates through an angle of \( \frac{5\pi}{6} \) radians. How far does a point on the rim travel?

hints.text: The distance a point on the rim travels equals the arc length: \( s = r\theta \).

solution_steps.text: The distance traveled by a point on the rim is the arc length: \( s = r\theta \).

problems.question_html: If \( \sin(\theta) = -\frac{3}{5} \) and \( \theta \) is in Quadrant IV, what is \( \cos(\theta) \)?

hints.text: Use the identity \( \sin^2(\theta) + \cos^2(\theta) = 1 \) and consider the sign of cosine in Quadrant IV.
\( \cos^2(\theta) = 1 - \frac{9}{25} = \frac{16}{25} \). In Quadrant IV, cosine is positive, so \( \cos(\theta) = \frac{4}{5} \).

solution_steps.text: Since \( \theta \) is in Quadrant IV, \( \cos(\theta) > 0 \), so \( \cos(\theta) = \frac{4}{5} \).

problems.question_html: The arc length formula is \( s = r\theta \). If the arc length is \( 12\pi \) cm and the radius is 8 cm, find the central angle \( \theta \) in radians.

hints.text: Rearrange the formula to solve for \( \theta \): \( \theta = \frac{s}{r} \).
\( \theta = \frac{12\pi}{8} = \frac{3\pi}{2} \).

problems.question_html:
A sprinkler rotates through an angle of \( \frac{2\pi}{3} \) radians and sprays water up to 15 meters from the sprinkler head.

(a) What is the arc length of the outer edge of the watered region?

(b) If the sprinkler rotates at a constant rate and completes one full rotation every 60 seconds, how long does it take to sweep through the \( \frac{2\pi}{3} \) radian sector?

(c) A point on the ground is 15 meters from the sprinkler at an angle of \( \frac{5\pi}{6} \) from the starting position of the sprinkler. Determine the coordinates of this point relative to the sprinkler (placed at the origin, starting along the positive \( x \)-axis).

hints.text: For (a), apply the arc length formula. For (b), think about what fraction of a full revolution the angle represents.
For (c), use \( x = r\cos(\theta) \) and \( y = r\sin(\theta) \) with \( r = 15 \) and \( \theta = \frac{5\pi}{6} \).

solution_steps.text: (b) The angle \( \frac{2\pi}{3} \) is \( \frac{1}{3} \) of a full revolution. Time \( = \frac{1}{3} \times 60 = 20 \) seconds.

problems.question_html:
A bicycle wheel has a diameter of 70 cm. A reflector is attached to the rim.

(a) The wheel rolls forward so that the reflector traces an arc of length 55 cm. Through what angle (in radians) has the wheel rotated?

(b) After the wheel rotates through \( \frac{3\pi}{4} \) radians from the starting position at \( (35, 0) \), find the coordinates of the reflector relative to the center of the wheel.

(c) In which quadrant does the reflector lie after the rotation in part (b)? State the signs of \( \sin(\theta) \) and \( \cos(\theta) \) for this angle.

hints.text: The radius is half the diameter. Use \( \theta = \frac{s}{r} \) for part (a).
For (b), use \( x = r\cos(\theta) \) and \( y = r\sin(\theta) \) with \( r = 35 \) and \( \theta = \frac{3\pi}{4} \). For (c), \( \frac{3\pi}{4} \) is in Quadrant II.

solution_steps.text: (c) The angle \( \frac{3\pi}{4} \) lies in Quadrant II, where \( \sin(\theta) > 0 \) and \( \cos(\theta) < 0 \).

concepts.title: Sine and Cosine Function Values
concepts.content_html:
Sine and Cosine Function Values

Certain angles on the unit circle produce exact values for sine and cosine that you must know from memory. These special angles appear throughout the AP Precalculus exam.

Special Angle Values

The key angles in the first quadrant and their sine and cosine values are:

\( \theta \)\( \cos(\theta) \)\( \sin(\theta) \)
\( 0 \)\( 1 \)\( 0 \)
\( \frac{\pi}{6} \)\( \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \)\( \frac{1}{2} \)
\( \frac{\pi}{4} \)\( \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \)\( \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \)
\( \frac{\pi}{3} \)\( \frac{1}{2} \)\( \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \)
\( \frac{\pi}{2} \)\( 0 \)\( 1 \)

Reference Angles

A reference angle is the acute angle formed between the terminal side of an angle and the \( x \)-axis. To evaluate sine or cosine of any angle:

  1. Find the reference angle \( \alpha \).
  2. Determine the sine and cosine of \( \alpha \) using the table above.
  3. Apply the correct sign based on the quadrant.

For example, to find \( \sin\!\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}\right) \): the reference angle is \( \pi - \frac{5\pi}{6} = \frac{\pi}{6} \). Since \( \frac{5\pi}{6} \) is in Quadrant II (sine positive), \( \sin\!\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}\right) = \sin\!\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = \frac{1}{2} \).

The Pythagorean Identity

For any angle \( \theta \):

\[ \sin^2(\theta) + \cos^2(\theta) = 1 \]

This identity follows directly from the equation of the unit circle \( x^2 + y^2 = 1 \). It is useful for finding one trig value when you know the other.

Worked Example

Find \( \cos\!\left(\frac{7\pi}{4}\right) \).

  1. Reference angle: \( 2\pi - \frac{7\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{4} \)
  2. \( \cos\!\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \)
  3. \( \frac{7\pi}{4} \) is in Quadrant IV, where cosine is positive.
  4. Therefore, \( \cos\!\left(\frac{7\pi}{4}\right) = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \).
AP Exam Tip: Memorize the unit circle values for all special angles. The AP exam expects exact values (like \( \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \)), not decimal approximations.

problem_sets.title: Practice: Sine and Cosine Function Values

problems.question_html: What is \( \sin\!\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) \)?

hints.text: Recall the special angle values from the unit circle for \( \frac{\pi}{3} \) (which is \( 60^\circ \)).
\( \sin\!\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \). Remember: \( \sin \) at \( 60^\circ \) is the larger value, \( \cos \) at \( 60^\circ \) is \( \frac{1}{2} \).

problems.question_html: What is \( \cos\!\left(\frac{5\pi}{3}\right) \)?

hints.text: Find the reference angle for \( \frac{5\pi}{3} \) and determine the quadrant.
Reference angle: \( 2\pi - \frac{5\pi}{3} = \frac{\pi}{3} \). Quadrant IV: cosine is positive. \( \cos\!\left(\frac{5\pi}{3}\right) = \cos\!\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{1}{2} \).

solution_steps.text: The reference angle is \( 2\pi - \frac{5\pi}{3} = \frac{\pi}{3} \). The angle \( \frac{5\pi}{3} \) is in Quadrant IV.
In Quadrant IV, cosine is positive: \( \cos\!\left(\frac{5\pi}{3}\right) = \cos\!\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{1}{2} \).

problems.question_html: Find the exact value of \( \sin\!\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}\right) \).

hints.text: The reference angle for \( \frac{3\pi}{4} \) is \( \pi - \frac{3\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{4} \). Is sine positive or negative in Quadrant II?
Sine is positive in Quadrant II. \( \sin\!\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}\right) = \sin\!\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \).

solution_steps.text: Reference angle: \( \pi - \frac{3\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{4} \). The angle is in Quadrant II, where sine is positive.

problems.question_html: Find the exact value of \( \cos\!\left(\frac{7\pi}{6}\right) \).

hints.text: Find the reference angle and determine the quadrant. What is the sign of cosine in that quadrant?
Reference angle: \( \frac{7\pi}{6} - \pi = \frac{\pi}{6} \). Quadrant III: cosine is negative. \( \cos\!\left(\frac{7\pi}{6}\right) = -\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \).

solution_steps.text: Reference angle: \( \frac{7\pi}{6} - \pi = \frac{\pi}{6} \). The angle is in Quadrant III.
Cosine is negative in Quadrant III: \( \cos\!\left(\frac{7\pi}{6}\right) = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \).

problems.question_html: If \( \cos(\theta) = \frac{5}{13} \) and \( \theta \) is in Quadrant I, what is \( \sin(\theta) \)?

hints.text: Use the Pythagorean identity \( \sin^2(\theta) + \cos^2(\theta) = 1 \).
\( \sin^2(\theta) = 1 - \frac{25}{169} = \frac{144}{169} \). Since \( \theta \) is in Quadrant I, \( \sin(\theta) = \frac{12}{13} \).

solution_steps.text: In Quadrant I, sine is positive: \( \sin(\theta) = \frac{12}{13} \).

problems.question_html: Which of the following angles has the same sine value as \( \frac{\pi}{4} \)?

hints.text: Sine is positive in Quadrants I and II. Which angle in Quadrant II has reference angle \( \frac{\pi}{4} \)?

\( \frac{3\pi}{4} \) is in Quadrant II with reference angle \( \pi - \frac{3\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{4} \). Since sine is positive in QII, \( \sin\!\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}\right) = \sin\!\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) \).

solution_steps.text: \( \sin\!\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \). We need another angle with the same sine value.
\( \frac{3\pi}{4} \) is in Quadrant II with reference angle \( \frac{\pi}{4} \), and sine is positive in QII: \( \sin\!\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}\right) = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \).

problems.question_html: If \( \sin(\theta) = -\frac{1}{2} \) and \( \pi < \theta < 2\pi \), find all possible values of \( \theta \). Enter the smaller value first, separated by a comma.

hints.text: Which special angle has \( \sin(\alpha) = \frac{1}{2} \)? Then find the angles in the given range where sine is negative.
\( \sin\!\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = \frac{1}{2} \). Sine is negative in QIII and QIV: \( \theta = \pi + \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{7\pi}{6} \) or \( \theta = 2\pi - \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{11\pi}{6} \).

solution_steps.text: Sine is negative in Quadrants III and IV. In QIII: \( \theta = \pi + \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{7\pi}{6} \). In QIV: \( \theta = 2\pi - \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{11\pi}{6} \).

problems.question_html: Use the Pythagorean identity to find \( \cos(\theta) \) given that \( \sin(\theta) = \frac{7}{25} \) and \( \theta \) is in Quadrant II.

hints.text: Apply \( \cos^2(\theta) = 1 - \sin^2(\theta) \), then choose the correct sign for Quadrant II.
\( \cos^2(\theta) = 1 - \frac{49}{625} = \frac{576}{625} \). Cosine is negative in QII: \( \cos(\theta) = -\frac{24}{25} \).

solution_steps.text: In Quadrant II, cosine is negative: \( \cos(\theta) = -\frac{24}{25} \).

problems.question_html:
Consider the angle \( \theta = \frac{11\pi}{6} \).

(a) Identify the quadrant in which \( \theta \) lies.

(b) Find the reference angle.

(c) Determine the exact values of \( \sin(\theta) \), \( \cos(\theta) \), and \( \tan(\theta) \).

hints.text: Determine where \( \frac{11\pi}{6} \) falls: is it between \( \frac{3\pi}{2} \) and \( 2\pi \)?
Reference angle \( = 2\pi - \frac{11\pi}{6} = \frac{\pi}{6} \). In QIV, cosine is positive and sine is negative.

problems.question_html:
A student claims that if \( \sin(\theta) = \frac{3}{5} \), then \( \cos(\theta) \) must equal \( \frac{4}{5} \).

(a) Explain why the student's claim is not necessarily true.

(b) Find all possible values of \( \cos(\theta) \) given \( \sin(\theta) = \frac{3}{5} \).

(c) For each value of \( \cos(\theta) \) found in part (b), identify the quadrant in which \( \theta \) lies and find \( \tan(\theta) \).
problems.correct_answer:
(a) The student forgot that cosine can be negative. Using the Pythagorean identity gives cos²(θ) = 16/25, so cos(θ) = ±4/5.
(b) cos(θ) = 4/5 or cos(θ) = -4/5.
(c) If cos(θ) = 4/5, then θ is in Quadrant I and tan(θ) = (3/5)/(4/5) = 3/4. If cos(θ) = -4/5, then θ is in Quadrant II and tan(θ) = (3/5)/(-4/5) = -3/4.

hints.text: The Pythagorean identity gives \( \cos^2(\theta) \), not \( \cos(\theta) \). Don't forget the square root produces two solutions.
\( \cos^2(\theta) = 1 - \frac{9}{25} = \frac{16}{25} \), so \( \cos(\theta) = \pm\frac{4}{5} \). Sine is positive in QI and QII.

solution_steps.text: (a) The Pythagorean identity gives \( \cos^2(\theta) = 1 - \frac{9}{25} = \frac{16}{25} \), so \( \cos(\theta) = \pm\frac{4}{5} \). The student assumed only the positive root.

concepts.title: Sine and Cosine Function Graphs
concepts.content_html:
Sine and Cosine Function Graphs

The graphs of \( y = \sin(x) \) and \( y = \cos(x) \) are smooth, continuous curves that repeat every \( 2\pi \) units. Understanding their key features is essential for analyzing more complex sinusoidal functions.

Graph of \( y = \sin(x) \)

The sine function starts at the origin, rises to a maximum of 1, returns to 0, drops to a minimum of \( -1 \), and returns to 0 to complete one cycle:

  • \( \sin(0) = 0 \)
  • \( \sin\!\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = 1 \) (maximum)
  • \( \sin(\pi) = 0 \)
  • \( \sin\!\left(\frac{3\pi}{2}\right) = -1 \) (minimum)
  • \( \sin(2\pi) = 0 \)

Graph of \( y = \cos(x) \)

The cosine function starts at its maximum, drops to 0, reaches its minimum, returns to 0, and returns to the maximum:

  • \( \cos(0) = 1 \) (maximum)
  • \( \cos\!\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = 0 \)
  • \( \cos(\pi) = -1 \) (minimum)
  • \( \cos\!\left(\frac{3\pi}{2}\right) = 0 \)
  • \( \cos(2\pi) = 1 \)

Key Features

  • Amplitude: The displacement from the midline to a maximum (or minimum). For both \( y = \sin(x) \) and \( y = \cos(x) \), the amplitude is 1.
  • Period: The horizontal length of one complete cycle: \( 2\pi \).
  • Midline: The horizontal line halfway between the maximum and minimum: \( y = 0 \).
  • Domain: All real numbers \( (-\infty, \infty) \).
  • Range: \( [-1, 1] \).
Key Idea: The amplitude measures the displacement from the midline, not the total distance from maximum to minimum. If the maximum is \( M \) and the minimum is \( m \), then the amplitude is \( \frac{M - m}{2} \) and the midline is \( y = \frac{M + m}{2} \).

Relationship Between Sine and Cosine

The cosine graph is a horizontal shift of the sine graph:

\[ \cos(x) = \sin\!\left(x + \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \]

This means the cosine curve leads the sine curve by \( \frac{\pi}{2} \) units.

Worked Example

Identify the amplitude, period, midline, and range of \( y = \sin(x) \).

  • Maximum value: 1. Minimum value: \( -1 \).
  • Amplitude: \( \frac{1 - (-1)}{2} = 1 \).
  • Midline: \( y = \frac{1 + (-1)}{2} = 0 \).
  • Period: \( 2\pi \) (one full cycle from 0 to \( 2\pi \)).
  • Range: \( [-1, 1] \).
AP Exam Tip: Use the term "displacement" rather than "distance" when describing how far a point is from the midline. Displacement accounts for direction (above or below), while distance does not.

problem_sets.title: Practice: Sine and Cosine Function Graphs

problems.question_html: What is the range of the function \( y = \cos(x) \)?

hints.text: Think about the maximum and minimum values that cosine can take on the unit circle.
The cosine function oscillates between \( -1 \) and \( 1 \), so the range is \( [-1, 1] \).

solution_steps.text: The maximum value of \( \cos(x) \) is 1 (at \( x = 0 \)) and the minimum is \( -1 \) (at \( x = \pi \)).

problems.question_html: At which of the following values of \( x \) does \( y = \sin(x) \) reach its minimum value?

hints.text: The minimum of \( \sin(x) \) is \( -1 \). At which key point on the unit circle does \( y = -1 \)?
\( \sin\!\left(\frac{3\pi}{2}\right) = -1 \), which is the minimum value.

solution_steps.text: This occurs at \( x = \frac{3\pi}{2} \) (and at \( x = \frac{3\pi}{2} + 2\pi k \) for any integer \( k \)).

problems.question_html: The period of \( y = \sin(x) \) is __________.

hints.text: The period is the horizontal length of one complete cycle.
One cycle of \( \sin(x) \) runs from \( 0 \) to \( 2\pi \). The period is \( 2\pi \).

solution_steps.text: The sine function completes one full cycle from \( x = 0 \) to \( x = 2\pi \).

problems.question_html: The amplitude of \( y = \cos(x) \) is __________.

hints.text: The amplitude is the displacement from the midline to the maximum.
The midline is \( y = 0 \) and the maximum is 1, so the amplitude is \( 1 - 0 = 1 \).

solution_steps.text: The maximum of \( \cos(x) \) is 1 and the minimum is \( -1 \). The midline is \( y = 0 \).

problems.question_html: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between the graphs of \( y = \sin(x) \) and \( y = \cos(x) \)?

choices.text: The cosine graph is a vertical shift of the sine graph by 1 unit.
The cosine graph is a horizontal shift of the sine graph by \( \frac{\pi}{2} \) units to the left.
The cosine graph is a reflection of the sine graph over the \( x \)-axis.
The cosine graph is a horizontal stretch of the sine graph by a factor of 2.

hints.text: Compare the values: \( \cos(0) = 1 = \sin\!\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) \). What kind of transformation relates these?
\( \cos(x) = \sin\!\left(x + \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \), which means the cosine graph is the sine graph shifted \( \frac{\pi}{2} \) to the left.

solution_steps.text: Since \( \cos(x) = \sin\!\left(x + \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \), the cosine function is the sine function shifted \( \frac{\pi}{2} \) units to the left.
This is a horizontal translation, not a vertical shift, reflection, or stretch.

problems.question_html: A sinusoidal function has a maximum value of 5 and a minimum value of \( -3 \). What are the amplitude and midline of this function?

hints.text: Amplitude \( = \frac{\text{max} - \text{min}}{2} \) and midline \( = \frac{\text{max} + \text{min}}{2} \).

solution_steps.text: Midline \( = \frac{\text{max} + \text{min}}{2} = \frac{5 + (-3)}{2} = 1 \). So the midline is \( y = 1 \).

problems.question_html: How many times does the graph of \( y = \sin(x) \) cross the \( x \)-axis on the interval \( [0, 4\pi] \)?

hints.text: The sine function equals zero at integer multiples of \( \pi \). List the multiples of \( \pi \) in \( [0, 4\pi] \).
\( \sin(x) = 0 \) at \( x = 0, \pi, 2\pi, 3\pi, 4\pi \). That is 5 zeros.

solution_steps.text: \( \sin(x) = 0 \) when \( x = n\pi \) for integer \( n \).

problems.question_html: The midline of a sinusoidal function with maximum 10 and minimum 2 is \( y = \) __________.

hints.text: The midline is the average of the maximum and minimum values.

problems.question_html:
Consider the graph of \( y = \cos(x) \) on the interval \( [0, 2\pi] \).

(a) State the coordinates of the maximum, minimum, and all zeros on this interval.

(b) Describe the intervals where the function is increasing and where it is decreasing.

(c) Explain why the domain of \( y = \cos(x) \) is all real numbers, while the range is \( [-1, 1] \).
problems.correct_answer:
(a) Maximum: (0, 1) and (2π, 1). Minimum: (π, -1). Zeros: (π/2, 0) and (3π/2, 0).
(b) Decreasing on (0, π) because cosine goes from 1 to -1. Increasing on (π, 2π) because cosine goes from -1 to 1.
(c) The input x can be any real number (any angle can be formed on the unit circle). The output is the x-coordinate of a point on the unit circle, which is always between -1 and 1.

hints.text: Evaluate \( \cos(x) \) at the key points \( 0, \frac{\pi}{2}, \pi, \frac{3\pi}{2}, 2\pi \).
Maximum at \( x = 0 \) and \( x = 2\pi \) (value 1). Minimum at \( x = \pi \) (value \( -1 \)). Zeros at \( x = \frac{\pi}{2} \) and \( x = \frac{3\pi}{2} \).

solution_steps.text: (c) Any real number can represent an angle, so the domain is \( (-\infty, \infty) \). Since \( \cos(x) \) is the \( x \)-coordinate on the unit circle, it satisfies \( -1 \leq \cos(x) \leq 1 \).

problems.question_html:
A student plots a sinusoidal function and observes the following: the graph reaches its highest point at \( (1, 8) \) and its lowest point at \( (5, 2) \).

(a) Determine the amplitude and midline of the function.

(b) Determine the period of the function.

(c) Explain whether this function could be modeled by a sine function starting at the midline, or a cosine function starting at its maximum. Write a possible equation for each.
problems.correct_answer:
(a) Amplitude = (8-2)/2 = 3. Midline: y = (8+2)/2 = 5.
(b) The distance from max to min is half a period: 5-1 = 4. Period = 2(4) = 8.
(c) Cosine starting at max: f(x) = 3cos((π/4)(x-1)) + 5. Sine starting at midline: since the midline crossing before the max at x=1 would be at x=1-2=-1, f(x) = 3sin((π/4)(x+1)) + 5.

hints.text: The distance from a maximum to the next minimum is half a period.
Amplitude \( = \frac{8 - 2}{2} = 3 \), midline \( y = 5 \), half-period \( = 5 - 1 = 4 \), so period \( = 8 \). Use \( b = \frac{2\pi}{\text{period}} = \frac{\pi}{4} \).

solution_steps.text: (b) From max at \( x = 1 \) to min at \( x = 5 \) is half a period: \( 5 - 1 = 4 \). Period \( = 8 \).

(c) Cosine form (max at \( x = 1 \)): \( f(x) = 3\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi}{4}(x - 1)\right) + 5 \). Sine form (midline crossing at \( x = -1 \), increasing): \( f(x) = 3\sin\!\left(\frac{\pi}{4}(x + 1)\right) + 5 \).

concepts.title: Sinusoidal Functions
concepts.content_html:
Sinusoidal Functions

A sinusoidal function is any function that can be written in the general form:

\[ f(\theta) = a\sin(b(\theta + c)) + d \quad \text{or} \quad f(\theta) = a\cos(b(\theta + c)) + d \]

The parameters \( a \), \( b \), \( c \), and \( d \) control the shape, size, and position of the graph.

Amplitude: \( |a| \)

The amplitude is \( |a| \), the displacement from the midline to the maximum (or minimum). If \( a < 0 \), the graph is reflected over the midline (the function starts by going down instead of up for sine).

Period: \( \frac{2\pi}{|b|} \)

The period is \( \frac{2\pi}{|b|} \). A larger \( |b| \) compresses the graph horizontally (shorter period), while a smaller \( |b| \) stretches it (longer period).

Phase Shift: \( -c \)

The phase shift (horizontal shift) is \( -c \). When \( c > 0 \), the graph shifts left by \( c \) units. When \( c < 0 \), the graph shifts right by \( |c| \) units. This is often written as \( f(\theta) = a\sin(b(\theta - h)) + d \), where \( h \) is the phase shift to the right.

Vertical Shift: \( d \)

The vertical shift \( d \) moves the midline to \( y = d \). The maximum becomes \( d + |a| \) and the minimum becomes \( d - |a| \).

Frequency

The frequency is the reciprocal of the period: \( \text{frequency} = \frac{|b|}{2\pi} \). It measures how many complete cycles occur per unit of the input variable.

Key Idea: Given any sinusoidal graph, you can read off the four parameters: amplitude \( = \frac{\text{max} - \text{min}}{2} \), midline \( = \frac{\text{max} + \text{min}}{2} \), period \( = \) distance for one cycle, and phase shift from where the standard cycle starts.

Worked Example

Write a sinusoidal function with amplitude 3, period \( \pi \), phase shift \( \frac{\pi}{4} \) to the right, and midline \( y = -2 \).

  1. \( a = 3 \) (amplitude)
  2. Period \( = \frac{2\pi}{|b|} = \pi \), so \( |b| = 2 \), take \( b = 2 \)
  3. Phase shift right by \( \frac{\pi}{4} \): use \( \theta - \frac{\pi}{4} \)
  4. \( d = -2 \) (vertical shift)

The function is: \( f(\theta) = 3\sin\!\left(2\!\left(\theta - \frac{\pi}{4}\right)\right) - 2 \).

AP Exam Tip: When reading the period from a graph, measure the full horizontal distance of one complete cycle. Then use \( |b| = \frac{2\pi}{\text{period}} \) to find \( b \). Do not confuse the period with the distance from a zero to a peak (which is only a quarter-period).

problems.question_html: What is the amplitude of \( f(x) = -4\sin(3x) + 1 \)?

hints.text: The amplitude is \( |a| \), the absolute value of the coefficient in front of sine.
Here \( a = -4 \), so the amplitude is \( |-4| = 4 \).

problems.question_html: What is the period of \( g(x) = 2\cos(5x) \)?

hints.text: The period formula is \( \frac{2\pi}{|b|} \). What is \( b \)?
\( b = 5 \), so the period is \( \frac{2\pi}{5} \).

problems.question_html: Find the midline of \( h(x) = 6\sin(x) - 3 \).

hints.text: The midline of \( a\sin(bx) + d \) is \( y = d \).
Here \( d = -3 \), so the midline is \( y = -3 \).

solution_steps.text: In \( h(x) = 6\sin(x) - 3 \), the vertical shift is \( d = -3 \).

problems.question_html: Find the period of \( f(\theta) = \sin\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right) \).

hints.text: Identify \( b \) in \( \sin(b\theta) \). Here the argument is \( \frac{\theta}{2} \), so \( b = \frac{1}{2} \).
Period \( = \frac{2\pi}{|b|} = \frac{2\pi}{1/2} = 4\pi \).

problems.question_html: Which function has amplitude 2, period \( \pi \), and midline \( y = 5 \)?

hints.text: Match amplitude \( = |a| = 2 \), midline \( = d = 5 \), and period \( = \frac{2\pi}{|b|} = \pi \).
Period \( = \pi \) means \( |b| = \frac{2\pi}{\pi} = 2 \). So \( f(x) = 2\sin(2x) + 5 \).

problems.question_html: The function \( f(x) = 3\cos\!\left(4\!\left(x - \frac{\pi}{8}\right)\right) + 1 \) has which phase shift?

hints.text: In the form \( a\cos(b(x - h)) + d \), the phase shift is \( h \) to the right.
Here \( h = \frac{\pi}{8} \), so the phase shift is \( \frac{\pi}{8} \) to the right.

solution_steps.text: The function is \( 3\cos\!\left(4\!\left(x - \frac{\pi}{8}\right)\right) + 1 \). Comparing to \( a\cos(b(x - h)) + d \), we have \( h = \frac{\pi}{8} \).
The phase shift is \( \frac{\pi}{8} \) units to the right.

problems.question_html: Find the maximum value of \( f(x) = -5\sin(2x) + 7 \).

hints.text: The maximum of \( a\sin(bx) + d \) is \( d + |a| \).

solution_steps.text: The amplitude is \( |a| = |-5| = 5 \) and the midline is \( y = 7 \).

problems.question_html: A sinusoidal function has period \( 6\pi \). What is the value of \( |b| \)?

hints.text: Use \( |b| = \frac{2\pi}{\text{period}} \).

problems.question_html:
A sinusoidal function has a maximum of 10 at \( x = 2 \) and a minimum of \( -4 \) at \( x = 8 \).

(a) Determine the amplitude, midline, and period.

(b) Write a cosine function that models this behavior.

(c) Write an equivalent sine function.
problems.correct_answer:
(a) Amplitude = (10-(-4))/2 = 7. Midline: y = (10+(-4))/2 = 3. Half-period = 8-2 = 6, so period = 12.
(b) b = 2π/12 = π/6. Max at x = 2, so cosine form: f(x) = 7cos((π/6)(x - 2)) + 3.
(c) Sine crosses midline (going up) a quarter-period before the max. Quarter-period = 3. So sine starts at x = 2-3 = -1: f(x) = 7sin((π/6)(x + 1)) + 3.

hints.text: The distance from max to min is half a period. Use the amplitude and midline formulas.
Amplitude 7, midline \( y = 3 \), period 12, \( b = \frac{\pi}{6} \). Cosine starts at max: shift right by 2. Sine starts at midline going up: shift right by \( 2 - 3 = -1 \).

solution_steps.text: (b) \( b = \frac{2\pi}{12} = \frac{\pi}{6} \). Cosine has max at \( x = 2 \): \( f(x) = 7\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi}{6}(x - 2)\right) + 3 \).
(c) Sine crosses the midline going up one quarter-period before the max: \( x = 2 - 3 = -1 \). So \( f(x) = 7\sin\!\left(\frac{\pi}{6}(x + 1)\right) + 3 \).

problems.question_html:
The function \( f(x) = a\sin(b(x + c)) + d \) has the following properties: amplitude 4, period \( 8\pi \), phase shift \( 2\pi \) to the left, and midline \( y = -1 \).

(a) Determine the values of \( a \), \( b \), \( c \), and \( d \).

(b) Write the complete equation of \( f(x) \).

(c) Find the maximum and minimum values of \( f(x) \), and identify one \( x \)-value where each occurs.
problems.correct_answer:
(a) a = 4 (amplitude). b = 2π/(8π) = 1/4. c = 2π (shift left by 2π). d = -1 (midline).
(b) f(x) = 4sin((1/4)(x + 2π)) - 1.
(c) Maximum = d + |a| = -1 + 4 = 3. This occurs when sin = 1, i.e., (1/4)(x + 2π) = π/2, so x + 2π = 2π, x = 0. Minimum = d - |a| = -1 - 4 = -5. This occurs when sin = -1, i.e., (1/4)(x + 2π) = 3π/2, so x + 2π = 6π, x = 4π.

hints.text: Match each parameter: \( |a| = 4 \), period \( = \frac{2\pi}{|b|} = 8\pi \), the phase shift formula gives \( c \), and \( d \) is the midline.

solution_steps.text: (a) \( |a| = 4 \), take \( a = 4 \). \( \frac{2\pi}{|b|} = 8\pi \) gives \( b = \frac{1}{4} \). Phase shift \( 2\pi \) left: \( c = 2\pi \). Midline: \( d = -1 \).
(c) Max \( = -1 + 4 = 3 \). Set \( \frac{1}{4}(x + 2\pi) = \frac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow x = 0 \). Min \( = -1 - 4 = -5 \). Set \( \frac{1}{4}(x + 2\pi) = \frac{3\pi}{2} \Rightarrow x = 4\pi \).

concepts.title: Sinusoidal Function Transformations
concepts.content_html:
Sinusoidal Function Transformations

In Topic 3.5, we introduced the general sinusoidal form \( f(\theta) = a\sin(b(\theta + c)) + d \). In this topic, we focus on how to apply and combine multiple transformations to produce or analyze sinusoidal graphs.

Order of Transformations

When graphing \( f(\theta) = a\sin(b(\theta + c)) + d \), apply transformations in the following order:

  1. Horizontal shift: Shift left by \( c \) (or right by \( -c \)).
  2. Horizontal compression/stretch: Compress or stretch by factor \( \frac{1}{|b|} \). The value \( b \) must satisfy \( b \neq 0 \).
  3. Vertical stretch/reflection: Stretch by \( |a| \) and reflect over the midline if \( a < 0 \).
  4. Vertical shift: Shift up by \( d \).
Key Idea: The parameter \( b \) must be nonzero (\( b \neq 0 \)). If \( b = 0 \), the expression \( \sin(0) \) is a constant, not a sinusoidal function.

Identifying Transformations from a Graph

Given a sinusoidal graph, read the transformations by identifying:

  • Midline: \( y = d \), found as the horizontal line halfway between maximum and minimum.
  • Amplitude: \( |a| = \frac{\text{max} - \text{min}}{2} \). If the graph is reflected (starts going down for sine), \( a < 0 \).
  • Period: Measure one full cycle, then \( |b| = \frac{2\pi}{\text{period}} \).
  • Phase shift: Determine how the starting point differs from the parent function.

Combining Transformations

Multiple transformations can act simultaneously. For example, the function \( f(x) = -3\cos\!\left(2\!\left(x - \frac{\pi}{4}\right)\right) + 5 \) involves:

  • Reflection over the midline (\( a = -3 < 0 \))
  • Vertical stretch by factor 3 (amplitude 3)
  • Horizontal compression (period \( = \frac{2\pi}{2} = \pi \))
  • Phase shift \( \frac{\pi}{4} \) to the right
  • Vertical shift up 5 (midline \( y = 5 \))

Worked Example

Describe the transformations of \( g(x) = 2\sin\!\left(3\!\left(x + \frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right) - 4 \) compared to \( y = \sin(x) \).

  • Amplitude: \( |2| = 2 \) (vertical stretch by 2)
  • Period: \( \frac{2\pi}{3} \) (horizontal compression by factor \( \frac{1}{3} \))
  • Phase shift: \( \frac{\pi}{6} \) to the left
  • Vertical shift: 4 units down (midline \( y = -4 \))

Key points of one cycle starting at \( x = -\frac{\pi}{6} \): midline \( \to \) max \( \to \) midline \( \to \) min \( \to \) midline, with \( x \)-values spaced \( \frac{1}{4} \cdot \frac{2\pi}{3} = \frac{\pi}{6} \) apart.

AP Exam Tip: When writing sinusoidal equations, always factor out \( b \) from the horizontal terms. Writing \( \sin(2x - \pi) \) is correct but harder to read than \( \sin\!\left(2\!\left(x - \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\right) \), which clearly shows the phase shift is \( \frac{\pi}{2} \) to the right.

problems.question_html: Which transformation converts \( y = \sin(x) \) into \( y = \sin(x) + 3 \)?

hints.text: Adding a constant outside the sine function shifts the graph vertically.
\( y = \sin(x) + 3 \) shifts the midline from \( y = 0 \) to \( y = 3 \), a vertical shift up 3.

solution_steps.text: The \( +3 \) is added outside the sine, which is a vertical transformation.
This shifts the entire graph up 3 units. The midline becomes \( y = 3 \).

problems.question_html: The function \( f(x) = \sin(4x) \) has been horizontally compressed compared to \( y = \sin(x) \). What is the period of \( f \)?

hints.text: Use \( \text{period} = \frac{2\pi}{|b|} \) with \( b = 4 \).
Period \( = \frac{2\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{2} \).

solution_steps.text: The graph completes 4 cycles in the same interval where \( \sin(x) \) completes 1.

problems.question_html: The function \( g(x) = -\cos(x) \) is obtained from \( y = \cos(x) \) by a reflection over the __________.

hints.text: The negative sign in front of cosine flips the graph vertically.
A negative \( a \) reflects the graph over the midline (the \( x \)-axis when \( d = 0 \)).

solution_steps.text: The negative sign (\( a = -1 \)) reflects every output: \( -\cos(x) \) flips the graph over the \( x \)-axis (the midline).
Maxima become minima and vice versa.

problems.question_html: The function \( h(x) = \cos\!\left(x - \frac{\pi}{3}\right) \) is a shift of \( y = \cos(x) \) by \( \frac{\pi}{3} \) units to the __________.

hints.text: In \( \cos(x - h) \), the graph shifts right by \( h \) units.
Here \( h = \frac{\pi}{3} \), so the shift is \( \frac{\pi}{3} \) to the right.

solution_steps.text: The form \( \cos(x - h) \) represents a horizontal shift right by \( h \).
With \( h = \frac{\pi}{3} \), the cosine graph shifts \( \frac{\pi}{3} \) to the right.

problems.question_html: Describe all transformations of \( y = -2\sin\!\left(3\!\left(x + \frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right) + 1 \) compared to \( y = \sin(x) \). What is the period?

choices.text: Period \( \frac{\pi}{3} \), amplitude 2, reflected, shifted left \( \frac{\pi}{6} \), up 1
Period \( \frac{2\pi}{3} \), amplitude 2, reflected, shifted left \( \frac{\pi}{6} \), up 1
Period \( 6\pi \), amplitude 2, reflected, shifted left \( \frac{\pi}{6} \), up 1

hints.text: Identify \( a = -2 \), \( b = 3 \), \( c = \frac{\pi}{6} \), \( d = 1 \) and compute the period.
Period \( = \frac{2\pi}{3} \). The negative \( a \) means reflection. \( c = \frac{\pi}{6} \) means shift left \( \frac{\pi}{6} \). \( d = 1 \) means shift up 1.

solution_steps.text: \( a = -2 \): amplitude 2 with reflection. \( b = 3 \): period \( = \frac{2\pi}{3} \).
\( c = \frac{\pi}{6} \): shift left \( \frac{\pi}{6} \). \( d = 1 \): shift up 1 (midline \( y = 1 \)).

problems.question_html: A cosine function has been vertically stretched by a factor of 5, horizontally stretched so its period is \( 4\pi \), and shifted down 2 units. Which equation represents this function?

hints.text: Vertical stretch by 5 means \( a = 5 \). Period \( 4\pi \) gives \( |b| = \frac{2\pi}{4\pi} = \frac{1}{2} \). Down 2 means \( d = -2 \).
\( y = 5\cos\!\left(\frac{1}{2}x\right) - 2 \).

problems.question_html: The function \( f(x) = 3\sin(2x - \pi) + 4 \) can be rewritten in the form \( a\sin(b(x - h)) + d \). What is the phase shift \( h \)?

hints.text: Factor out the \( b \) from the argument: \( 2x - \pi = 2(x - ?) \).
\( 2x - \pi = 2\!\left(x - \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \), so the phase shift is \( h = \frac{\pi}{2} \) to the right.

solution_steps.text: The phase shift is \( h = \frac{\pi}{2} \) (to the right).

problems.question_html: The function \( g(x) = a\cos(b(x - h)) + d \) has maximum 9, minimum 1, and period \( \frac{\pi}{3} \). Find \( |a| \) and \( |b| \).

hints.text: Amplitude \( = \frac{9-1}{2} \). Period \( = \frac{2\pi}{|b|} = \frac{\pi}{3} \).

problems.question_html:
The graph of a sinusoidal function passes through the points \( (0, 3) \), \( (2, 7) \), \( (4, 3) \), \( (6, -1) \), and \( (8, 3) \).

(a) Determine the amplitude, midline, and period.

(b) Write a cosine equation for this function.

(c) Verify your equation by checking that it gives the correct value at \( x = 6 \).
problems.correct_answer:
(a) Max = 7, min = -1. Amplitude = (7-(-1))/2 = 4. Midline = (7+(-1))/2 = 3. From max at x=2 to next max: we need one full cycle. Max to min is half-period: 6-2 = 4, period = 8.
(b) b = 2π/8 = π/4. Max at x = 2 so cosine form: f(x) = 4cos((π/4)(x-2)) + 3.
(c) f(6) = 4cos((π/4)(6-2)) + 3 = 4cos(π) + 3 = 4(-1) + 3 = -1. ✓ Matches the data.

hints.text: Identify the maximum and minimum from the data points to find amplitude and midline. Then find the period.
Max \( = 7 \) at \( x = 2 \), min \( = -1 \) at \( x = 6 \). Amplitude 4, midline 3, period 8. Use cosine centered at the max.

solution_steps.text: (c) \( f(6) = 4\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi}{4}(4)\right) + 3 = 4\cos(\pi) + 3 = 4(-1) + 3 = -1 \). This matches the data point \( (6, -1) \).

problems.question_html:
Two students are asked to write an equation for a sinusoidal graph with amplitude 3, period \( \pi \), midline \( y = 2 \), and a maximum at \( x = \frac{\pi}{4} \).

Student A writes: \( f(x) = 3\cos\!\left(2\!\left(x - \frac{\pi}{4}\right)\right) + 2 \)

Student B writes: \( f(x) = 3\sin\!\left(2x\right) + 2 \)

(a) Verify that Student A's equation has the correct amplitude, period, midline, and maximum location.

(b) Does Student B's equation also satisfy all four requirements? Justify your answer.

(c) Write a third equation using \( -\sin \) that also satisfies all four requirements.
problems.correct_answer:
(a) Student A: a=3 (amplitude 3 ✓), b=2 (period = 2π/2 = π ✓), d=2 (midline y=2 ✓). At x=π/4: f(π/4) = 3cos(0)+2 = 5 = 2+3 (max ✓). All correct.
(b) Student B: amplitude 3 ✓, period π ✓, midline y=2 ✓. Max occurs when sin(2x) = 1, so 2x = π/2, x = π/4. Max at x = π/4 ✓. Student B is also correct.
(c) Using -sin: max occurs when -sin = -1, which is when sin = 1... but -sin max is 1 not at sin=1. In fact, -sin reaches max when sin = -1, i.e., 2x = 3π/2, x = 3π/4. We need max at x = π/4: f(x) = -3sin(2(x - π/2)) + 2, since -sin(2(π/4 - π/2)) = -sin(-π/2) = -(-1) = 1. ✓

hints.text: Verify each equation by checking amplitude (\( |a| \)), period (\( \frac{2\pi}{|b|} \)), midline (\( d \)), and the \( x \)-value where the maximum occurs.
For the \( -\sin \) version, the maximum occurs when \( \sin = -1 \). Shift so that \( \sin = -1 \) happens at \( x = \frac{\pi}{4} \).

solution_steps.text: (a) Student A: \( |a| = 3 \), period \( = \frac{2\pi}{2} = \pi \), midline \( y = 2 \). At \( x = \frac{\pi}{4} \): \( f = 3\cos(0) + 2 = 5 \) (max). All correct.
(b) Student B: \( |a| = 3 \), period \( = \pi \), midline \( y = 2 \). Max when \( \sin(2x) = 1 \): \( 2x = \frac{\pi}{2} \), \( x = \frac{\pi}{4} \). All four properties match.

(c) For \( -\sin \): maximum occurs when \( -\sin = 1 \), i.e., \( \sin = -1 \). We need \( 2\!\left(\frac{\pi}{4} - h\right) = -\frac{\pi}{2} \), giving \( h = \frac{\pi}{2} \). Equation: \( f(x) = -3\sin\!\left(2\!\left(x - \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\right) + 2 \).

concepts.title: Sinusoidal Function Context and Data Modeling
concepts.content_html:
Sinusoidal Function Context and Data Modeling

Many real-world phenomena are periodic and can be modeled with sinusoidal functions. In this topic, we apply the sinusoidal form \( f(t) = a\sin(b(t + c)) + d \) or \( f(t) = a\cos(b(t + c)) + d \) to real-world contexts.

Common Periodic Contexts

  • Temperature: Average daily or monthly temperatures follow an approximately sinusoidal pattern over one year (period \( \approx 12 \) months or 365 days).
  • Tides: Water levels rise and fall with a period of approximately 12.4 hours.
  • Ferris wheels: The height of a rider varies sinusoidally with a period equal to the time for one revolution.
  • Daylight hours: The number of daylight hours varies sinusoidally over one year.

Building a Sinusoidal Model from Data

To construct a sinusoidal model from data:

  1. Identify the midline: \( d = \frac{\text{max} + \text{min}}{2} \).
  2. Identify the amplitude: \( |a| = \frac{\text{max} - \text{min}}{2} \).
  3. Identify the period: Measure the time for one complete cycle. Then \( b = \frac{2\pi}{\text{period}} \).
  4. Identify the phase shift: Determine where the maximum or midline crossing occurs and adjust \( c \) accordingly.

Sinusoidal Regression

When real data does not perfectly fit a sinusoidal curve, a graphing calculator or statistical software can perform sinusoidal regression to find the best-fit parameters \( a \), \( b \), \( c \), and \( d \). This is analogous to linear regression but for periodic data.

Worked Example

A city's average monthly temperature (in \( ^\circ\text{F} \)) has a maximum of \( 88^\circ\text{F} \) in July (month 7) and a minimum of \( 38^\circ\text{F} \) in January (month 1). Model the temperature as a function of month \( t \).

  1. Midline: \( d = \frac{88 + 38}{2} = 63 \)
  2. Amplitude: \( |a| = \frac{88 - 38}{2} = 25 \)
  3. Period: 12 months, so \( b = \frac{2\pi}{12} = \frac{\pi}{6} \)
  4. Using cosine with maximum at \( t = 7 \): \( T(t) = 25\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi}{6}(t - 7)\right) + 63 \)

We can verify: \( T(7) = 25\cos(0) + 63 = 88 \) and \( T(1) = 25\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi}{6}(-6)\right) + 63 = 25\cos(-\pi) + 63 = 25(-1) + 63 = 38 \). Both check out.

AP Exam Tip: When modeling real-world periodic data, always verify your equation by plugging in known data points. The AP exam frequently asks you to interpret parameters in context (e.g., "the 25 represents the temperature varies 25 degrees above and below the average").
